## Client-Side Tools: Memory

The memory tool enables Claude to store and retrieve information across conversations through a memory file directory. Claude can create, read, update, and delete files that persist between sessions.

### Key Facts

- Client-side tool — you control storage via your implementation
- Supports commands: `view`, `create`, `str_replace`, `insert`, `delete`, `rename`
- Operates on files in a `/memories` directory
- The Python, TypeScript, and Java SDKs provide helper classes/functions for implementing the memory backend

> **Security:** Never store API keys, passwords, tokens, or other secrets in memory files. Be cautious with personally identifiable information (PII) — check data privacy regulations (GDPR, CCPA) before persisting user data. The reference implementations have no built-in access control; in multi-user systems, implement per-user memory directories and authentication in your tool handlers.

For full implementation examples, use WebFetch:

- Docs: `https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/memory-tool.md`

---

## Client-Side Tools: Bash and Text Editor

The bash and text editor tools are **Anthropic-defined, schema-less** tools. Declare them by `type` and `name` only — the input schema is built into the model and cannot be modified. **Do not pass an `input_schema`**, and do not define a custom tool that happens to be named `"bash"` — that creates a user-defined tool without the built-in behavior.

Both are **client-executed**: Claude returns a `tool_use` block, your code performs the action locally, and you send back a `tool_result`. The API is stateless; your application maintains the shell session or filesystem between turns.

### Bash tool declaration

```json
{"type": "bash_20250124", "name": "bash"}
```

| Language | Declaration |
|---|---|
| Python / TypeScript / Ruby / cURL | plain object `{"type": "bash_20250124", "name": "bash"}` |
| Go | `anthropic.ToolUnionParam{OfBashTool20250124: &anthropic.ToolBash20250124Param{}}` |
| Java | `.addTool(ToolBash20250124.builder().build())` from `com.anthropic.models.messages` |
| C# | `Tools = [new ToolBash20250124()]` from `Anthropic.Models.Messages` |
| PHP | `tools: [new \Anthropic\Messages\ToolBash20250124()]` |

Claude's `tool_use.input` contains either `{"command": "<string>"}` or `{"restart": true}`. Check for `restart` first (reset the session, return a confirmation string); otherwise run `command` and return combined stdout + stderr.

> **Security — commands are untrusted model output.** Run in an isolated environment (container, VM, or restricted user); apply an **allowlist** of permitted executables and reject shell operators (`&&`, `|`, `;`, `` ` ``, `$()`); set timeouts and resource limits; log every command. A blocklist is not sufficient.

### Text editor tool declaration

```json
{"type": "text_editor_20250728", "name": "str_replace_based_edit_tool"}
```

Optional field: `max_characters` to cap `view` output. Java exposes a typed `ToolTextEditor20250728` builder (`com.anthropic.models.messages`); other statically-typed SDKs follow the same naming pattern — see the Anthropic-Defined Tools section in `{lang}/claude-api/tool-use.md` for the exact class.

> **Security — `path` is untrusted model output. Confine every file operation to a fixed project root.** Before executing any command, resolve the model-supplied `path` to its canonical form and verify it remains within your project root; reject the request if it escapes (`..`, symlinks, absolute paths outside the root, URL-encoded traversal like `%2e%2e%2f`). Use your language's built-in path utilities (e.g., Python `pathlib.Path.resolve()` then check `.is_relative_to(root)`). Never call `open()` / `writeFile` / `unlink` directly on the raw `path` value.

`tool_use.input.command` is one of:

| `command` | Other inputs | Action |
|---|---|---|
| `view` | `path`, optional `view_range` | Return file contents or directory listing |
| `create` | `path`, `file_text` | Create/overwrite file with `file_text`. Create a backup if the file already exists. |
| `str_replace` | `path`, `old_str`, `new_str` | Replace exactly one occurrence; error if 0 or >1 matches |
| `insert` | `path`, `insert_line`, `insert_text` | Insert `insert_text` after line `insert_line` (0 = beginning of file) |

For both tools, on error return `{"type": "tool_result", "tool_use_id": "…", "content": "<error text>", "is_error": true}` so Claude can recover.

## Structured Outputs

Structured outputs constrain Claude's responses to follow a specific JSON schema, guaranteeing valid, parseable output. This is not a separate tool — it enhances the Messages API response format and/or tool parameter validation.

Two features are available:

- **JSON outputs** (`output_config.format`): Control Claude's response format
- **Strict tool use** (`strict: true`): Guarantee valid tool parameter schemas

**Supported models:** Claude Fable 5, Claude Opus 5, Claude Opus 4.8, Claude Sonnet 5, and Claude Haiku 4.5. Legacy models (Claude Opus 4.5, Claude Opus 4.1) also support structured outputs.

> **Recommended:** Use `client.messages.parse()` which automatically validates responses against your schema. When using `messages.create()` directly, use `output_config: {format: {...}}`. The `output_format` convenience parameter is also accepted by some SDK methods (e.g., `.parse()`), but `output_config.format` is the canonical API-level parameter.

### JSON Schema Limitations

**Supported:**

- Basic types: object, array, string, integer, number, boolean, null
- `enum`, `const`, `anyOf`, `allOf`, `$ref`/`$def`
- String formats: `date-time`, `time`, `date`, `duration`, `email`, `hostname`, `uri`, `ipv4`, `ipv6`, `uuid`
- `additionalProperties: false` (required for all objects)

**Not supported:**

- Recursive schemas
- Numerical constraints (`minimum`, `maximum`, `multipleOf`)
- String constraints (`minLength`, `maxLength`)
- Complex array constraints
- `additionalProperties` set to anything other than `false`

The Python and TypeScript SDKs automatically handle unsupported constraints by removing them from the schema sent to the API and validating them client-side.

### Important Notes

- **First request latency**: New schemas incur a one-time compilation cost. Subsequent requests with the same schema use a 24-hour cache.
- **Refusals**: If Claude refuses for safety reasons (`stop_reason: "refusal"`), the output may not match your schema.
- **Token limits**: If `stop_reason: "max_tokens"`, output may be incomplete. Increase `max_tokens`.
- **Incompatible with**: Citations (returns 400 error), message prefilling.
- **Works with**: Batches API, streaming, token counting, extended thinking.

## Tips for Effective Tool Use

1. **Provide detailed descriptions**: Claude relies heavily on descriptions to understand when and how to use tools
2. **Use specific tool names**: `get_current_weather` is better than `weather`
3. **Validate inputs**: Always validate tool inputs before execution
4. **Handle errors gracefully**: Return informative error messages so Claude can adapt
5. **Limit tool count**: Too many tools can confuse the model — keep the set focused
6. **Test tool interactions**: Verify Claude uses tools correctly in various scenarios

For detailed tool use documentation, use WebFetch:

- URL: `https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/overview`
</doc>

## When to Use WebFetch

Use WebFetch to get the latest documentation when:

- User asks for "latest" or "current" information
- Cached data seems incorrect
- User asks about features not covered here

Live documentation URLs are in `shared/live-sources.md`.

## Common Pitfalls

- Don't truncate inputs when passing files or content to the API. If the content is too long to fit in the context window, notify the user and discuss options (chunking, summarization, etc.) rather than silently truncating.
- **Prefill removed (Fable 5, Opus 5, Sonnet 5, and the 4.6/4.7/4.8 family):** Assistant message prefills (last-assistant-turn prefills) return a 400 error on Fable 5, Opus 5, Sonnet 5, Opus 4.6, Opus 4.7, Opus 4.8, and Sonnet 4.6. Use structured outputs (`output_config.format`) or system prompt instructions to control response format instead. (One exception: the fallback-credit prefill claim — when redeeming a credit with `fallback_has_prefill_claim: true`, the server accepts the echoed assistant message; see the migration guide's refusal section.)
- **Confirm migration scope before editing:** When a user asks to migrate code to a newer Claude model without naming a specific file, directory, or file list, **ask which scope to apply first** — the entire working directory, a specific subdirectory, or a specific set of files. Do not start editing until the user confirms. Imperative phrasings like "migrate my codebase", "move my project to X", "upgrade to Sonnet 4.6", or bare "migrate to Opus 4.8" are **still ambiguous** — they tell you what to do but not where, so ask. Proceed without asking only when the prompt names an exact file, a specific directory, or an explicit file list ("migrate `app.py`", "migrate everything under `services/`", "update `a.py` and `b.py`"). See `shared/model-migration.md` Step 0.
- **`max_tokens` defaults:** Don't lowball `max_tokens` — hitting the cap truncates output mid-thought and requires a retry. For non-streaming requests, default to `~16000` (keeps responses under SDK HTTP timeouts). For streaming requests, default to `~64000` (timeouts aren't a concern, so give the model room). Only go lower when you have a hard reason: classification (`~256`), cost caps, deliberately short outputs, or **`max_tokens: 0`** for cache pre-warming (see `shared/prompt-caching.md` → Pre-warming).
- **Disabling thinking on Claude Opus 5 has two failure modes — prefer low/medium effort instead.** Only affects code that explicitly opts out; thinking is on by default, so watch for a disabled-thinking setting carried forward from Opus 4.8. With `thinking: {type: "disabled"}`, the model occasionally writes a tool call into its **visible text** instead of a `tool_use` block: the turn succeeds, the call never runs, no error is raised, and in an agentic loop that text pollutes later turns. It can also leak `<thinking>` tags into the response. Turning thinking on and lowering `effort` fixes both and still cuts cost. If a route must stay thinking-off: add *"You may say a brief sentence before using a tool"*, **delete** any don't-think/don't-reason rule (it makes tag leakage worse), and use a generic *"Do not include internal or system XML tags in your response"* rather than naming thinking tags. Details: `shared/model-migration.md` → Two failure modes when thinking is disabled.
- **128K output tokens:** Fable 5, Opus 5, Opus 4.6, Opus 4.7, Opus 4.8, Sonnet 5, and Sonnet 4.6 support up to 128K `max_tokens`, but the SDKs require streaming for values that large to avoid HTTP timeouts. Use `.stream()` with `.get_final_message()` / `.finalMessage()`.
- **Tool call JSON parsing (Fable 5, Opus 5, and the 4.6/4.7/4.8 family):** Fable 5, Opus 5, Opus 4.6, Opus 4.7, Opus 4.8, and Sonnet 4.6 may produce different JSON string escaping in tool call `input` fields (e.g., Unicode or forward-slash escaping). Always parse tool inputs with `json.loads()` / `JSON.parse()` — never do raw string matching on the serialized input.
- **Structured outputs (all models):** Use `output_config: {format: {...}}` instead of the deprecated `output_format` parameter on `messages.create()`. This is a general API change, not 4.6-specific.
- **Don't reimplement SDK functionality:** The SDK provides high-level helpers — use them instead of building from scratch. Specifically: use `stream.finalMessage()` instead of wrapping `.on()` events in `new Promise()`; use typed exception classes (`Anthropic.RateLimitError`, etc.) instead of string-matching error messages; use SDK types (`Anthropic.MessageParam`, `Anthropic.Tool`, `Anthropic.Message`, etc.) instead of redefining equivalent interfaces.
- **Error handling — catch a chain, not one broad class.** A single `except APIStatusError` / `catch (AnthropicServiceException)` / `rescue APIError` loses the distinction between retryable (429, ≥500, network) and non-retryable (400/404) failures. Write a most-specific-first chain — e.g. `NotFoundError` → `RateLimitError` → `APIStatusError` → `APIConnectionError` (or the Go equivalent: `errors.As` into `*anthropic.Error` then `switch apierr.StatusCode { case 404: …; case 429: …; default: … }`). Per-language class names and namespaces are in `shared/error-codes.md`.
- **Don't research SDK types — write first.** If a type name isn't shown in the documentation included in this skill, write the code file from the namespace/package tables in the language-specific doc and let the compiler's error point you to the right name. Do not spend turns on WebFetch, SDK-repo clones, or compiling-and-running a separate reflection program to discover type names before writing — produce the source file first, then fix what the compiler reports. A quick `strings` / `jar tf` / `javap` against the installed SDK is acceptable for locating names (it returns in seconds), but don't escalate beyond that. A file with a wrong type name is recoverable; a session spent on discovery with no file written is not.
- **Bash and text editor tools are Anthropic-defined, schema-less.** Declare `{"type": "bash_20250124", "name": "bash"}` / `{"type": "text_editor_20250728", "name": "str_replace_based_edit_tool"}` — no `input_schema`. A custom tool with your own schema named `"bash"` is a different tool. Handler paths and security checks are in `shared/tool-use-concepts.md` § Client-Side Tools.
- **Advisor tool model pairing.** The advisor tool's `model` must be at least as capable as the request's top-level `model` — e.g. executor `claude-sonnet-5` → advisor `claude-opus-4-8` or `claude-opus-4-7`. An invalid pair returns 400. Pairing table in `shared/tool-use-concepts.md` § Advisor. Availability: `shared/platform-availability.md`.
- **Agent Skills ≠ Managed Agents.** To have Claude generate a `.pptx`/`.xlsx`/etc. via Agent Skills, call `client.beta.messages.create` with `container={"skills": [...]}`, the `code_execution_20260521` tool, and both `code-execution-2025-08-25` + `skills-2025-10-02` betas. Do not use `client.beta.agents` / `sessions` / `environments` here — those are the Managed Agents surface, not Agent Skills.
- **MCP connector needs both halves.** `mcp_servers=[{type:"url", url, name}]` alone is rejected as a validation error — also add `tools=[{type:"mcp_toolset", mcp_server_name:<same name>}]` with beta `mcp-client-2025-11-20`. Availability: `shared/platform-availability.md`.
- **`inference_geo` is a direct top-level request parameter** — `client.messages.create(..., inference_geo="us")` / `.inferenceGeo("us")`. Do not put it in `extra_body` / `putAdditionalBodyProperty`. (Messages API only — on Managed Agents, `inference_geo` instead nests inside the agent's `model` object, never top-level; see `shared/managed-agents-core.md` § Pinning inference geography.) Supported on Opus 4.6 / Sonnet 4.6 and later; availability: `shared/platform-availability.md`. `response.usage.inference_geo` reports where inference ran.
- **Fine-grained tool streaming is not a beta feature.** Set `eager_input_streaming: true` on the tool definition and call the regular `client.messages.stream(...)`. There is no beta header and no `client.beta.*` path.
- **Cache diagnostics is beta.** Use `client.beta.messages.*` with beta `cache-diagnosis-2026-04-07`. Pass `diagnostics: {previous_message_id: null}` on the first turn and `diagnostics: {previous_message_id: <previous response id>}` on subsequent turns; the result is on `response.diagnostics`. Availability: `shared/platform-availability.md`.
- **Memory tool type is `memory_20250818`.** Declare `{"type": "memory_20250818", "name": "memory"}`. Go uses the beta-namespace type `{OfMemoryTool20250818: &anthropic.BetaMemoryTool20250818Param{}}` on `client.Beta.Messages.New`; Python/TypeScript/Ruby/PHP/C# use the non-beta `client.messages.create`; Java has both a non-beta `MemoryTool20250818` and a beta tool-runner path. Python/TypeScript provide `BetaAbstractMemoryTool` / `betaMemoryTool` helpers for implementing the backend.
- **Use a model the feature actually supports.** Some features are restricted to specific model tiers — fast mode is Claude Opus 5 / Opus 4.8 only (and Claude API only), task budgets (Messages API only — Managed Agents session budgets have no model-tier restriction) are Claude Opus 5 / Fable 5 / Sonnet 5 / Opus 4.8 / 4.7 only, and the advisor tool requires a valid executor↔advisor pair. If the user's prompt names a model that the feature doesn't support, use a supported model instead and note the substitution in the output.
- **Don't define custom types for SDK data structures:** The SDK exports types for all API objects. Use `Anthropic.MessageParam` for messages, `Anthropic.Tool` for tool definitions, `Anthropic.ToolUseBlock` / `Anthropic.ToolResultBlockParam` for tool results, `Anthropic.Message` for responses. Defining your own `interface ChatMessage { role: string; content: unknown }` duplicates what the SDK already provides and loses type safety.
- **Report and document output:** For tasks that produce reports, documents, or visualizations, the code execution sandbox has `python-docx`, `python-pptx`, `matplotlib`, `pillow`, and `pypdf` pre-installed. Claude can generate formatted files (DOCX, PDF, charts) and return them via the Files API — consider this for "report" or "document" type requests instead of plain stdout text.
- **Server-tool errors don't raise.** Web search and web fetch errors return HTTP 200 with a `web_search_tool_result` / `web_fetch_tool_result` block whose `content` is a single error object (e.g. `{error_code: "max_uses_exceeded"}`) — not a raised exception. For web search, a success `content` is a *list*; an error `content` is an *object* — branch on that before indexing.
- **Code execution output block type:** `code_execution_20260521` returns `bash_code_execution_tool_result` (with `.content.stdout`), **not** the legacy bare `code_execution_tool_result`. Iterate `response.content` and match on the correct type.
- **Tool search: never defer everything.** The search tool itself must not have `defer_loading: true`, and at least one tool in `tools` must be non-deferred, or the API returns 400 `All tools have defer_loading set`.

# chezmoi-dotfiles

This machine's `$HOME` is managed by a **chezmoi** (configs) + **ansible** (system
deps) dotfiles repo. This skill is the agent-facing map: how to drive it, and what
custom tooling exists that you wouldn't otherwise know about. It is rendered per-host
— the "What's enabled on THIS machine" section reflects what the user actually
selected at init.

## Orientation (read this first)

- **Repo root**: `chezmoi source-path` (no args) prints the source dir. Work there
  to edit: `cd "$(chezmoi source-path)"`.
- **Source path of one file**: `chezmoi source-path ~/.config/foo/bar` → the
  managed source file for that target.
- **`docs/**` is NOT deployed to `$HOME`** (it's chezmoi-ignored). Read detail via
  `"$(chezmoi source-path)/docs/..."`. A *subset* is deployed to `~/.config/docs/`
  (e.g. keybindings, cli-tools) for runtime helpers.
- **Read the contract before editing**: `"$(chezmoi source-path)/CLAUDE.md"` holds
  Hard invariants and cross-file maintenance rules. Honor them.
- This host: profile `macos`, OS `darwin`/`amd64`, primary shell `zsh`.

## chezmoi essentials

```bash
chezmoi diff                 # preview changes (also: just chezmoi-diff)
chezmoi apply                # deploy + run scripts (also: cas, or just chezmoi-apply)
chezmoi status               # modified/added/removed targets
chezmoi edit ~/.zshrc        # edit the SOURCE of a target
chezmoi add  ~/.config/x     # start managing an existing file
chezmoi re-add               # pull live edits back into source
chezmoi managed | grep foo   # is X managed?
chezmoi cat ~/.config/x      # render a target without applying
chezmoi data | jq            # the template data (ground truth for the toggles below)
```

- **`cas`** = `chezmoi apply` + reload hint; **`cau`** = update from remote then apply
  (defined in `dot_config/shell/99_chezmoi_reload.sh`).
- **`dotcfg`** = reconfigure the init prompts on an already-set-up machine
  (`dotcfg` for the TUI, `dotcfg --set installLlmTools=true --yes` for one toggle,
  `dotcfg --dry-run` to preview). Shell twin: `czcfg`.
- **Never `chezmoi add` a `modify_`/`create_` target** — it overwrites the script.
- Full command cheat-sheet: `docs/this_repo/cheatsheet.md`. Install-vs-upgrade is
  split: `chezmoi apply`/ansible is **install-only**; upgrades go through
  `just upgrade-*`.

- **Vim mode** — shell modal editing + tmux vim nav (NOT Neovim/editors — those are always vim).

## Custom in-house CLIs (always deployed to `~/.dotfiles/bin`, on PATH)

Each works from any cwd. Run with `--help`. Most have `docs/tools/<name>.md`, but not all (`x` → `clipboard.md`, `view-ebook` → `yazi-previews.md`, `fleet` → `this_repo/fleet-apply.md`); grep `docs/` if the obvious path 404s. Full list: `ls "$(chezmoi source-path)/dot_dotfiles/bin/"`.

- **`fleet`** — cross-host ops over your machines: `fleet chezmoi apply`, `fleet hosts`, `fleet tmux`, `fleet info`, `fleet pueue`, `fleet exec`. See `docs/this_repo/fleet-apply.md`, `docs/tools/fleet-exec.md`, `docs/tools/fleet-hosts.md`.
- **`mlf`** — MLflow umbrella CLI + TUI dashboard (needs Python uv tools). Picker twin: `tv mlflow`.
- **`pqsum`** — pueue queue summary (text / AI / JSON). See `docs/tools/pueue.md`.
- **`x`** — clipboard/file copy-paste-open with cross-platform fallbacks.
- **`view-office`** / **`view-ebook`** — open/preview Office docs (.docx/.xlsx/.pptx + legacy .doc/.xls/.ppt) and ebooks (epub/mobi/azw3, calibre-backed) in the terminal; also power the yazi previewers. See `docs/tools/office-viewers.md`, `docs/tools/yazi-previews.md`.
- **`mi-router`** / **`reyee`** / **`sms`** — read-only router CLIs (Xiaomi MiWiFi / Ruijie Reyee / Huawei HiLink SMS). See `docs/tools/{mi-router,reyee,sms}.md`.
- **`mi-dhcp-bind`** — opt-in **write** companion to `mi-router`: set/remove MiWiFi static DHCP reservations (`bind --self` autodetects this host). See `docs/tools/mi-dhcp-bind.md`.
- **`ping-monitor`** — record ping over time, flag latency spikes. See `docs/tools/ping-monitor.md`.
- **`wake`** — Wake-on-LAN sender: `wake <host>` powers a box on by magic packet (hosts in `~/.config/wake/hosts.toml`). Passive side = `installWakeOnLan` ansible role. See `docs/sysadmin/wake-on-lan.md`.
- **`tsnet`** — Tailscale helper: `tsnet list` (tailnet devices, `--tsv`/`--json`), `tsnet ssh-config <machine>` (idempotent managed block in `~/.ssh/config.d/20-tailscale`; detects the legacy no-`Include` case and shadowing `Host` blocks, both of which make ssh config silently inert), `tsnet serve <port>` (preflight → `tailscale serve --bg --https=443` → verify, for services that hard-require an `https://` origin), `tsnet doctor`. `--host H` drives any of it on a remote box over ssh. Picker twin: `tv tailnet`. See `docs/tools/tsnet.md`.
- **`agent-warmup`** — drive a real interactive agent TUI at a scheduled time to move the quota window (launchd/systemd/pueue). See `docs/tools/agent-warmup.md`.
- **`crash-blackbox`** — flight recorder for hard power-offs / unclean shutdowns. See `docs/tools/crash-blackbox.md`.
- **`nvidia-driver-drift-check`** — flag kernel-module vs userspace driver drift. See `docs/sysadmin/gpu-driver.md`.
- **`yth`** — search your YouTube watch history (title/channel/description + captions; Takeout import + optional cookie sync). Picker twin: `tv yth`. See `docs/tools/yth.md`.
- **`appsrc`** — detect how an installed app / CLI was installed & managed (cask / App Store / direct-download / apt / snap / flatpak / AppImage / cargo/npm/pipx/uv/mise/go/gem / manual): `appsrc which <cmd-or-app>` (live), `appsrc size <app>` (footprint + associated cache/data/containers), `appsrc tui` (interactive dashboard — sort by size, filter), bare `appsrc` / `appsrc scan` (cached inventory, `--json`/`--tsv`/`--size`/`--sort`). Picker twins: `tv appsrc` (by source) / `tv appsrc-size` (by footprint). See `docs/tools/appsrc.md`.
- **`herdr-grep`** — search visible or retained content across panes in the current, one named, or all running local Herdr sessions; reports exact session/workspace/tab/pane coordinates, supports `--json`, and `--pick` pipes matches to fzf then exact-focuses/attaches the selection. Inside Herdr, `prefix+Alt+F` opens a visible-content picker (Alt+S = scrollback, Alt+V = visible). Remote use runs the CLI through SSH. See `docs/tools/herdr.md`.
- **`dotcfg`** — reconfigure dotfiles prompts (above).
- **`sesh-preview`** — preview helper for the sesh picker.

**`herdr`** is a first-class managed surface too (config in `dot_config/herdr/`, upgrade via `just upgrade-herdr` — which must NOT be run from inside a herdr pane): a remote pane/workspace server with three metadata pickers (`tv herdr-agent-panes`, `tv herdr-review`, `tv herdr-sesh`) plus `herdr-grep` for pane-content search. See `docs/tools/herdr.md` and the herdr entries in `pitfalls/`. Distinct from `wt` (worktrunk) and `wm` (workmux).

## Television (`tv`) — fuzzy pickers with custom channels

There are ~50 **custom** channels (system state, fleet, services, infra, agents…)
that you won't discover otherwise. Browse them:

```bash
tv                      # default picker
tv list-channels        # list everything available
tv <channel>            # open one, e.g. tv fleet-hosts | tv mlflow | tv pueue
ls "$(chezmoi source-path)/dot_config/television/cable/"   # the channel definitions
```

Handy ones: `fleet-hosts`, `tailnet`, `ssh-config`, `mlflow`, `pueue`, `ports`,
`kill-process`, `services`, `sessions`, `keybindings`, `aliases`, `git-ops`,
`mac-apps`/`linux-apps`, the agent trio (`agent-panes`, `agent-sessions`,
`agent-wakeup`) and the `herdr-*` family. Full reference: `docs/tools/tv.md`.

## Keybindings & keymaps

- **`bindings`** (shell function) or **`tv keybindings`** — interactive reference.
- **tmux**: `prefix + Space` opens the action menu. There is **no `prefix + e`** —
  that alias was removed, and `prefix + E` is "break every pane into its own
  window", so do not guess it. `prefix + T` = sesh picker, `prefix + U` = tools.
  Deep ref: `docs/tools/tmux/keybindings.md`.
- **shell ZLE widgets**: `Alt+S` sesh sessions, `Alt+T` tools, `Ctrl+R` history (atuin).
- Master reference: `docs/shells/keybindings.md` (also deployed to `~/.config/docs/shells/keybindings.md`).

## Aliases & functions

`alias` to list shell aliases, or `tv aliases`. Catalog: `docs/shells/aliases.md`.
Helpers worth knowing: `chezmoi-cd` (jump to source), `run-for` (time-box a command),
`bindings` (above). App control: `applaunch`/`appquit`/`apprestart`/… (cross-platform).
System audio (cross-platform, built-in): `sysvol`/`sysmute` (+ `sysplay`/`sysnow` with `installMediaControl`); remote mute via `fleet exec --login -- sysmute on`.

## just recipes (run from the source dir)

```bash
cd "$(chezmoi source-path)" && just --list
```

Categories: `chezmoi-*`, `ansible-*`, `upgrade-*` (brew/mise/uv/npm/cargo/…),
`fleet`/`fleet-*`, `gen-prompts` (regenerate prompt scaffolding), `check`/`lint`,
`docker-*`. See `docs/this_repo/cheatsheet.md`.

## Editing rules (don't skip)

Before changing anything under the repo, read `CLAUDE.md` Hard invariants and the
"Cross-file maintenance rules" table — many surfaces have mandatory mirror updates
in the same commit (docs, completions, tool-managers index, this very skill, …).

1	# Copilot.psm1 — GitHub Copilot agent gateway for Claude Code and Codex, native
2	# PowerShell port of the POSIX 43_copilot_proxy.sh / 44_copilot_embed.sh.
3	#
4	# Runs the maintained copilot-api fork (npm @jeffreycao/copilot-api) via `bunx`
5	# so a GitHub Copilot subscription can back Claude Code and Codex. The optional Bun
6	# throttle shim (copilot-throttle-shim.js) is reused verbatim from the unix side.
7	#
8	# Public commands (exported with their original hyphenated names for muscle
9	# memory — PSUseApprovedVerbs is intentionally waived):
10	#   copilot-proxy [start|stop|restart|status|doctor [--live]|logs [shim|N]|shim [on|off|status]|whoami|auth|reinstall]
11	#   copilot-run <cmd...>            run a command with the proxy env injected
12	#   claude-copilot [args...]        one-off Claude Code session on the proxy
13	#   claude-copilot-once [args...]   pinned one-shot session, auto-reverted
14	#   codex-copilot [args...]         one-off Codex session on Responses proxy
15	#   codex-copilot-once [args...]    identical zero-persistence alias
16	# (claude-copilot / -once run claude with --dangerously-skip-permissions — the
17	#  proxy flow is the trusted, hands-off path; plain `claude` is unaffected.)
18	#   copilot-here [on|off|status]    per-project pin via ./.claude/settings.local.json
19	#   copilot-model [<id>|-l|-c|--auto]  switch the pinned model
20	#   copilot-embed [--model M] [--json] [TEXT|-] | -l
21	#   semsearch index [PATH...] | semsearch <QUERY> [-k N] [--corpus PATH]
22	#
23	# Contract preserved from the unix version: token at
24	# ~/.local/share/copilot-api/github_token, ports 4141 (proxy) / 4142 (shim),
25	# state under $XDG_STATE_HOME/copilot-proxy, per-project ./.claude/settings.local.json
26	# pin, default model gpt-5.6-sol[1m], and the ANTHROPIC_* env block.
27	#
28	# The pinned package is INSTALLED ONCE into $XDG_DATA_HOME/copilot-api/pkg and the
29	# proxy runs that binary directly. It deliberately does NOT use `bunx` at launch:
30	# bunx re-resolves the package on every start, and bun stalls forever resolving
31	# through a socks proxy — which wedged `start` at "Resolving dependencies" AND kept
32	# bun's global cache lock, so every retry hung too. Force a re-install with
33	# `copilot-proxy reinstall`.
34	#
35	# Env knobs:
36	#   COPILOT_PROXY_PORT   default 4141    - port the proxy listens on
37	#   COPILOT_PROXY_START_TIMEOUT default 45 - seconds allowed for model refresh
38	#   COPILOT_SHIM_PORT    default 4142    - throttle shim port
39	#   COPILOT_API_PKG      default @jeffreycao/copilot-api@2.1.0 - spec to install
40	#                                          (changing it re-installs via the stamp)
41	#   COPILOT_CLAUDE_MODEL                 - override the pinned model
42	#   COPILOT_PROXY_QUIET  1               - add the telemetry-suppressing env keys
43	#   COPILOT_INSTALL_NOPROXY 1            - skip straight to the no-proxy install try
44	#   COPILOT_HTTP_PROXY   default auto    - Node->GitHub /models egress:
45	#                          auto   = use the Windows System Proxy (WinINET registry)
46	#                                   or HTTPS_PROXY when either is set; Node ignores
47	#                                   the system setting unless it is passed the env.
48	#                          always = same, but warn when no proxy is found
49	#                          never  = never pass --proxy-env
50	#                          http://127.0.0.1:PORT = force that URL

54	# ------------------------------------------------------------------ helpers ---
55	function script:Get-CopilotPort { if ($env:COPILOT_PROXY_PORT) { $env:COPILOT_PROXY_PORT } else { '4141' } }
56	function script:Get-CopilotPkg  { if ($env:COPILOT_API_PKG)   { $env:COPILOT_API_PKG }   else { '@jeffreycao/copilot-api@2.1.0' } }

70	# --- pinned package install (run the binary, never `bunx` at launch) -----------
71	#
72	# Why an install prefix instead of `bunx <pkg> start`: bunx re-resolves the
73	# package on EVERY launch, and bun hangs indefinitely resolving through a socks
74	# proxy (a browser/curl through the same proxy is fine, which is what makes it so
75	# confusing). The wedged installer then keeps bun's global install-cache lock, so
76	# every retry hangs identically and stacks another zombie. Installing once and
77	# running the resulting binary removes the per-start resolve entirely — a warm
78	# start does zero network before it binds the port.
79	
80	# Package NAME without the trailing @version, keeping any @scope/ prefix.
81	# The naive "split on @" eats the whole string on a scoped spec with no version
82	# (@jeffreycao/copilot-api -> ""), so test on the scope-stripped copy.
83	function script:Get-CopilotPkgName {
84	    $spec = Get-CopilotPkg
85	    if ($spec.TrimStart('@') -match '@') { $spec -replace '@[^@]*$', '' } else { $spec }
86	}

88	function script:Get-CopilotPkgPrefix { Join-Path (Get-XdgData) 'copilot-api/pkg' }
89	# Records the spec the prefix currently holds, so bumping COPILOT_API_PKG (or the
90	# pinned default) re-installs instead of silently running the old version.
91	function script:Get-CopilotPkgStamp { Join-Path (Get-CopilotPkgPrefix) '.installed-spec' }

94	# (plus a .bunx sidecar); the other extensions cover an npm/yarn-populated prefix.
95	# Returns $null when no directly-runnable shim exists — Get-CopilotPkgLaunch then
96	# falls back to `bun run`, which resolves from the local node_modules offline.
97	function script:Get-CopilotPkgBin {
98	    $binDir = Join-Path (Get-CopilotPkgPrefix) 'node_modules/.bin'
99	    foreach ($ext in '.exe', '.cmd', '.bat', '', '.ps1') {
100	        $p = Join-Path $binDir "copilot-api$ext"
101	        if (Test-Path -LiteralPath $p -PathType Leaf) { return $p }
102	    }
103	    $null
104	}

106	# How to invoke the installed proxy: @{ Exe; Pre; Cwd }. Cwd is non-null only for
107	# the `bun run` fallback, which must resolve node_modules/.bin from the prefix.
108	#
109	# The prefix is deliberately NOT passed as an argument (`bun run --cwd <path>`):
110	# Start-Process joins -ArgumentList with spaces and does no quoting, so a prefix
111	# under a $HOME containing a space ("C:\Users\Da-Wei Lee\...") would arrive split
112	# across two argv entries. -WorkingDirectory takes the path as a real parameter.
113	function script:Get-CopilotPkgLaunch {
114	    $bin = Get-CopilotPkgBin

116	    # shell script — route both through `bun run`, which finds node_modules/.bin.
117	    if ($bin -and [System.IO.Path]::GetExtension($bin) -in '.exe', '.cmd', '.bat') {
118	        return @{ Exe = $bin; Pre = @(); Cwd = $null }
119	    }
120	    if (Get-Command bun -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue) {

142	# One package-install attempt in -Dir, bounded by -BudgetSeconds. npm is preferred
143	# because it supports Azure Artifacts' credential-provider token in ~/.npmrc;

155	function script:Invoke-CopilotPkgInstallTry {

157	
158	    $proxyVars = 'ALL_PROXY', 'all_proxy', 'HTTP_PROXY', 'http_proxy', 'HTTPS_PROXY', 'https_proxy'

165	    }

167	    if ($NoProxy) {

169	    }

171	        $p = Start-Process -FilePath $installer.File -ArgumentList $installer.Args `
172	            -WorkingDirectory $Dir -PassThru -NoNewWindow -ErrorAction Stop
173	        if ($p.WaitForExit($BudgetSeconds * 1000)) { return (Test-CopilotPkgPresent) }
174	        Stop-Process -Id $p.Id -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
175	        # The subshell's child is the one actually holding the install lock.
176	        $name = [regex]::Escape((Get-CopilotPkgName))

178	            Where-Object { $_.Name -in 'bun.exe', 'node.exe' -and $_.CommandLine -match '\b(add|install)\b' -and $_.CommandLine -match $name } |
179	            ForEach-Object { Stop-Process -Id $_.ProcessId -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue }
180	        return $false
181	    } catch {
182	        Write-Error "copilot-proxy: could not launch package installer ($_)"; return $false
183	    } finally {
184	        if ($NoProxy) {
185	            foreach ($v in $proxyVars) { if ($null -ne $saved[$v]) { Set-Item "env:$v" $saved[$v] } }
186	        }
187	    }
188	}

190	# Ensure the pinned spec is installed. No-op (and no network) once it is.
191	function script:Install-CopilotPkg {
192	    if (Test-CopilotPkgReady) { return $true }
193	    if (-not (Get-Command bun -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue)) {
194	        Write-Error "copilot-proxy: bun not found (scoop install bun)"; return $false
195	    }
196	    $spec = Get-CopilotPkg; $prefix = Get-CopilotPkgPrefix
197	    New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path $prefix | Out-Null
198	    # A private package.json keeps `bun add` from walking up and polluting $HOME.
199	    $pkgJson = Join-Path $prefix 'package.json'
200	    if (-not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $pkgJson)) {
201	        '{"name":"copilot-api-runner","private":true,"version":"0.0.0"}' | Set-Content -Path $pkgJson -Encoding utf8
202	    }
203	
204	    Write-Host "copilot-proxy: installing $spec (one-time — later starts skip this) ..."
205	    # Attempt 1 honours the ambient env: on a host where the npm registry is only
206	    # reachable THROUGH the proxy, stripping it would break the install. Attempt 2
207	    # strips it, which is what rescues the socks stall. COPILOT_INSTALL_NOPROXY=1
208	    # skips straight to attempt 2 (saves the 45s stall on a known-bad host).
209	    $skipFirst = ($env:COPILOT_INSTALL_NOPROXY -eq '1')
210	    if ($skipFirst -or -not (Invoke-CopilotPkgInstallTry -Dir $prefix -BudgetSeconds 45)) {
211	        if (-not $skipFirst) {
212	            Write-Warning "copilot-proxy: install stalled with the proxy env — retrying without it ..."
213	            # Drop bun's cache lock dir before retrying; the killed attempt may have
214	            # left it behind, and a stale lock hangs the retry for the same reason.
215	            $bunHome = if ($env:BUN_INSTALL) { $env:BUN_INSTALL } else { Join-Path $HOME '.bun' }
216	            Remove-Item -Recurse -Force (Join-Path $bunHome 'install/cache/.tmp') -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
217	        }
218	        if (-not (Invoke-CopilotPkgInstallTry -Dir $prefix -NoProxy -BudgetSeconds 90)) {
219	            Write-Error "copilot-proxy: could not install $spec — run 'copilot-proxy doctor'."; return $false
220	        }
221	    }
222	
223	    if (-not (Test-CopilotPkgPresent) -or -not (Get-CopilotPkgLaunch)) {
224	        Write-Error "copilot-proxy: install finished but no runnable copilot-api under $prefix."; return $false
225	    }
226	    $spec | Set-Content -Path (Get-CopilotPkgStamp) -Encoding utf8
227	    $true
228	}

230	# Run a copilot-api subcommand (auth / check-usage / debug) in the foreground.
231	# Honours $launch.Cwd so the `bun run` fallback resolves node_modules/.bin.
232	function script:Invoke-CopilotPkgCommand {
233	    param([Parameter(ValueFromRemainingArguments)] [string[]] $Argument)
234	    if (-not (Install-CopilotPkg)) { return }
235	    $launch = Get-CopilotPkgLaunch
236	    if (-not $launch) { Write-Error "copilot-proxy: no runnable copilot-api — try 'copilot-proxy reinstall'"; return }
237	    if ($launch.Cwd) { Push-Location $launch.Cwd }
238	    try { & $launch.Exe @($launch.Pre + $Argument) }
239	    finally { if ($launch.Cwd) { Pop-Location } }
240	}

242	# Live `bun add … copilot-api` processes. Install is a one-shot, so a match at
243	# rest is a clean stale-installer signal: a stalled one keeps bun's global
244	# install-cache lock, which wedges every later install too. Invoke-CopilotPkgInstallTry
245	# bounds and kills its own attempts, so this should stay empty — it remains as a
246	# safety net for a stall we didn't spawn (e.g. a hand-run `bunx @jeffreycao/copilot-api`).
247	function script:Get-CopilotStaleInstaller {
248	    Get-CimInstance Win32_Process -Filter "Name = 'bun.exe'" -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue |
249	        Where-Object { $_.CommandLine -match '\badd\b' -and $_.CommandLine -match 'copilot-api' }
250	}

262	# --- egress: which proxy should Node use for the GitHub /models fetch? --------
263	#
264	# copilot-api fetches /models ONCE at startup and caches it for the whole process
265	# lifetime, and GitHub geo-filters the Claude catalog on some egress paths. Node
266	# does NOT honour the Windows System Proxy on its own — it only sees HTTP(S)_PROXY
267	# — so a host whose browser reaches the unfiltered catalog could still have the
268	# proxy cache a Claude-less list, which then looks exactly like an entitlement
269	# problem. Resolve the URL here and hand it to the child explicitly.
270	#
271	# COPILOT_HTTP_PROXY: auto|always|never|<url>. Returns a URL or $null.
272	function script:Resolve-CopilotHttpProxy {
273	    $mode = if ($env:COPILOT_HTTP_PROXY) { $env:COPILOT_HTTP_PROXY } else { 'auto' }
274	    switch -Regex ($mode) {
275	        '^(never|off|0|false|no)$' { return $null }
276	        '^(http|https|socks5h?)://' { return $mode }
277	        '^(always|auto|on|1|true|yes)$' { break }
278	        default {
279	            Write-Warning "copilot-proxy: unknown COPILOT_HTTP_PROXY='$mode' (use auto|always|never|http://...)"
280	            return $null
281	        }
282	    }
283	
284	    # The Windows System Proxy (WinINET). This is what Clash Verge / mihomo /
285	    # v2rayN write when their "System Proxy" toggle is on, so reading it covers
286	    # the same ground the unix side gets from its Clash detector.
287	    try {
288	        $key = Get-ItemProperty -Path 'HKCU:\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Internet Settings' -ErrorAction Stop
289	        if ($key.ProxyEnable -eq 1 -and $key.ProxyServer) {
290	            # ProxyServer is either "host:port" or "http=host:port;https=host:port".
291	            $server = $key.ProxyServer
292	            if ($server -match '(?:^|;)\s*https?=([^;]+)') { $server = $Matches[1] }
293	            elseif ($server -match ';') { $server = ($server -split ';')[0] }
294	            if ($server) { return "http://$($server -replace '^https?://', '')" }
295	        }
296	    } catch { $null = $_ }
297	
298	    # Fallback: an explicit env proxy in this shell.
299	    foreach ($v in $env:HTTPS_PROXY, $env:https_proxy, $env:HTTP_PROXY, $env:http_proxy) {
300	        if ($v) { return $v }
301	    }
302	    $null
303	}
304	
305	# Model ids GitHub serves for this account RIGHT NOW, for the direct-vs-proxied
306	# A/B in doctor. -Via: 'direct' forces no proxy, a URL forces that proxy, absent
307	# uses .NET defaults. Returns sorted-unique ids, or $null on any failure.
308	#
309	# Secrets: the ghu_/bearer tokens only ever travel in request headers — never in
310	# a command line, never echoed.
311	function script:Get-CopilotUpstreamModel {
312	    param([string] $Via)
313	
314	    $tokFile = Get-CopilotToken
315	    if (-not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $tokFile)) { return $null }
316	    $ghu = Get-Content -First 1 $tokFile -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
317	    if (-not $ghu) { return $null }
318	
319	    $transport = @{}
320	    if ($Via -eq 'direct') { $transport['NoProxy'] = $true }
321	    elseif ($Via) { $transport['Proxy'] = $Via }
322	
323	    try {
324	        $ex = Invoke-RestMethod -Uri 'https://api.github.com/copilot_internal/v2/token' -TimeoutSec 10 `
325	            -Headers @{ 'Authorization' = "token $ghu"; 'user-agent' = 'GitHubCopilotChat/0.26.7' } `
326	            @transport -ErrorAction Stop
327	    } catch { return $null }
328	
329	    $api = if ($ex.endpoints.api) { $ex.endpoints.api } else { 'https://api.githubcopilot.com' }
330	    if (-not $ex.token) { return $null }
331	
332	    try {
333	        $up = Invoke-RestMethod -Uri "$api/models" -TimeoutSec 12 `
334	            -Headers @{
335	                'Authorization'            = "Bearer $($ex.token)"
336	                'user-agent'               = 'GitHubCopilotChat/0.26.7'
337	                'copilot-integration-id'   = 'vscode-chat'
338	            } @transport -ErrorAction Stop
339	    } catch { return $null }
340	
341	    @($up.data.id | Where-Object { $_ } | Sort-Object -Unique)
342	}

344	# Optional ChatGPT Apps reachability. This is deliberately separate from the
345	# Copilot inference probes: codex_apps is a remote MCP served by chatgpt.com,
346	# not a localhost bridge to Codex.app and not part of GitHub Copilot.
347	function script:Get-CopilotProbeFailureKind {
348	    param($ErrorRecord)
349	
350	    $message = if ($ErrorRecord -is [System.Management.Automation.ErrorRecord]) {
351	        $ErrorRecord.Exception.ToString()
352	    } else { [string]$ErrorRecord }
353	
354	    if ($message -match '(?i)timed?\s*out|timeout|operation.*canceled|deadline') { return 'timeout' }
355	    if ($message -match '(?i)certificate|authenticationexception|ssl|tls|secure channel') { return 'tls' }
356	    'network'
357	}

359	function script:Invoke-CopilotOptionalHttpProbe {
360	    param(
361	        [Parameter(Mandatory)] [string] $Uri,
362	        [string] $Via = 'direct'
363	    )
364	
365	    $transport = @{}
366	    if ($Via -eq 'direct') { $transport['NoProxy'] = $true }
367	    elseif ($Via) { $transport['Proxy'] = $Via }
368	
369	    $sw = [System.Diagnostics.Stopwatch]::StartNew()
370	    try {
371	        $response = Invoke-WebRequest -Uri $Uri -Method Get -TimeoutSec 12 `
372	            -SkipHttpErrorCheck -Headers @{ 'user-agent' = 'codex-copilot-doctor/1.0' } `
373	            @transport -ErrorAction Stop
374	        $sw.Stop()
375	        [pscustomobject]@{
376	            Reached = $true
377	            Code    = [int]$response.StatusCode
378	            Seconds = [math]::Round($sw.Elapsed.TotalSeconds, 2)
379	            Kind    = $null
380	            Error   = $null
381	        }
382	    } catch {
383	        $sw.Stop()
384	        [pscustomobject]@{
385	            Reached = $false
386	            Code    = 0
387	            Seconds = [math]::Round($sw.Elapsed.TotalSeconds, 2)
388	            Kind    = Get-CopilotProbeFailureKind $_
389	            Error   = ($_.Exception.Message -replace '\s+', ' ').Trim()
390	        }
391	    }
392	}

418	# Resolve the model: $COPILOT_CLAUDE_MODEL > state file > default.
419	#
420	#   - HYPHENATED ids (claude-opus-4-8), not dotted (claude-opus-4.8): Claude Code
421	#     only recognizes hyphenated family names — dotted ids fall back to a legacy
422	#     "[Opus 4] retired" label AND a 200k context assumption.
423	#   - "[1m]" suffix: Claude Code uses it to size HUD/compaction for a 1M context
424	#     window. ConvertTo-CopilotClaudeModel derives it from live /v1/models metadata
425	#     for every provider. Claude Code-only: raw API clients use the plain id.
426	function script:Get-CopilotDefaultModel {
427	    if ($env:COPILOT_CLAUDE_MODEL) { return $env:COPILOT_CLAUDE_MODEL }
428	    $sf = Get-CopilotModelState
429	    if (Test-Path $sf) { return (Get-Content -First 1 $sf) }
430	    'gpt-5.6-sol[1m]'
431	}

433	# Every model id the proxy accepts: .id plus the .claude_model_id alias.
434	function script:Get-CopilotServedModels {
435	    try { $r = Invoke-RestMethod -Uri "$(Get-CopilotBase)/v1/models" -TimeoutSec 5 -ErrorAction Stop } catch { return @() }
436	    $ids = [System.Collections.Generic.List[string]]::new()
437	    foreach ($m in $r.data) {
438	        if ($m.id) { $ids.Add($m.id) }
439	        if ($m.claude_model_id) { $ids.Add($m.claude_model_id) }
440	    }
441	    $ids | Sort-Object -Unique
442	}

462	# Convert a raw proxy id to the spelling Claude Code should receive. A live
463	# max_context_window_tokens >= 1M earns [1m]. Offline, preserve an explicitly
464	# stored suffix but do not invent one.
465	function script:ConvertTo-CopilotClaudeModel {
466	    param([Parameter(Mandatory)] [string] $Model, $Catalog)
467	    $hadHint = $Model -match '\[1m\]$'
468	    $raw = Remove-CopilotContextHint $Model
469	    if (-not $PSBoundParameters.ContainsKey('Catalog')) { $Catalog = Get-CopilotModelCatalog }
470	    if ($Catalog) {
471	        $entry = $Catalog.data | Where-Object { $_.id -eq $raw } | Select-Object -First 1
472	        $context = $entry.capabilities.limits.max_context_window_tokens
473	        if ($context -and [long]$context -ge 1000000) { return "$raw[1m]" }
474	        return $raw
475	    }
476	    if ($hadHint) { return "$raw[1m]" }
477	    $raw
478	}

482	    foreach ($c in $Candidate) { if ($Model -contains $c) { return $c } }
483	    $null
484	}

486	# Build the complete Claude Code role profile for a selected main model. Native
487	# Claude profiles use the strongest served model in each family. OpenAI profiles
488	# map quality/balanced/fast work to the selected main, Terra and Luna.
489	function script:Get-CopilotModelProfile {
490	    param([string] $Model = (Get-CopilotDefaultModel), $Catalog)
491	    if (-not $PSBoundParameters.ContainsKey('Catalog')) { $Catalog = Get-CopilotModelCatalog }
492	    $models = Get-CopilotCatalogIds $Catalog
493	    $raw = Remove-CopilotContextHint $Model
494	    $main = ConvertTo-CopilotClaudeModel -Model $Model -Catalog $Catalog
495	
496	    $fableRaw = $raw; $opusRaw = $raw; $sonnetRaw = $raw; $haikuRaw = $raw
497	    if ($raw -like 'claude-*') {
498	        $fableRaw = Select-CopilotFirstServed -Model $models -Candidate @('claude-fable-5')
499	        if (-not $fableRaw) { $fableRaw = @($models | Where-Object { $_ -like 'claude-fable-*' } | Sort-Object)[-1] }
500	        if (-not $fableRaw) { $fableRaw = $raw }
501	
502	        $opusRaw = Select-CopilotFirstServed -Model $models -Candidate @(
503	            'claude-opus-5', 'claude-opus-4-8', 'claude-opus-4-7', 'claude-opus-4-6', 'claude-opus-4-5'
504	        )
505	        if (-not $opusRaw) { $opusRaw = @($models | Where-Object { $_ -like 'claude-opus-*' } | Sort-Object)[-1] }
506	        if (-not $opusRaw) { $opusRaw = $raw }
507	
508	        $sonnetRaw = Select-CopilotFirstServed -Model $models -Candidate @(
509	            'claude-sonnet-5', 'claude-sonnet-4-6', 'claude-sonnet-4-5'
510	        )
511	        if (-not $sonnetRaw) { $sonnetRaw = @($models | Where-Object { $_ -like 'claude-sonnet-*' } | Sort-Object)[-1] }
512	        if (-not $sonnetRaw) { $sonnetRaw = $raw }
513	
514	        $haikuRaw = Select-CopilotFirstServed -Model $models -Candidate @('claude-haiku-4-5')
515	        if (-not $haikuRaw) { $haikuRaw = @($models | Where-Object { $_ -like 'claude-haiku-*' } | Sort-Object)[-1] }
516	        if (-not $haikuRaw) { $haikuRaw = $raw }
517	    }
518	    elseif ($raw -like 'gpt-*' -or $raw -match 'codex') {
519	        $sonnetRaw = Select-CopilotFirstServed -Model $models -Candidate @('gpt-5.6-terra')
520	        if (-not $sonnetRaw) { $sonnetRaw = $raw }
521	        $haikuRaw = Select-CopilotFirstServed -Model $models -Candidate @('gpt-5.6-luna', 'gpt-5.4-mini', 'gpt-5-mini')
522	        if (-not $haikuRaw) { $haikuRaw = $raw }
523	    }
524	
525	    [ordered]@{
526	        main   = $main
527	        fable  = ConvertTo-CopilotClaudeModel -Model $fableRaw -Catalog $Catalog
528	        opus   = ConvertTo-CopilotClaudeModel -Model $opusRaw -Catalog $Catalog
529	        sonnet = ConvertTo-CopilotClaudeModel -Model $sonnetRaw -Catalog $Catalog
530	        haiku  = ConvertTo-CopilotClaudeModel -Model $haikuRaw -Catalog $Catalog
531	    }
532	}

538	    Write-Host ("  opus   : {0}" -f $ModelProfile.opus)
539	    Write-Host ("  sonnet : {0}" -f $ModelProfile.sonnet)

543	# "<model>|<source>" — the model Claude Code would send from this directory.
544	function script:Get-CopilotEffectiveModel {
545	    $settings = '.claude/settings.local.json'
546	    if (Test-Path $settings) {
547	        try {
548	            $j = Get-Content -Raw $settings | ConvertFrom-Json
549	            if ($j.env.ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL) {
550	                $m = $j.env.ANTHROPIC_MODEL
551	                if ($m) { return "$m|project pin: $settings" }
552	            }
553	        } catch { $null = $_ }
554	    }
555	    if ($env:COPILOT_CLAUDE_MODEL) { return "$($env:COPILOT_CLAUDE_MODEL)|`$COPILOT_CLAUDE_MODEL" }
556	    $sf = Get-CopilotModelState
557	    if (Test-Path $sf) { return "$(Get-Content -First 1 $sf)|state file: $sf" }
558	    "$(Get-CopilotDefaultModel)|built-in default"

561	# The EXACT env block `copilot-here on` / `copilot-run` would apply right now.
562	#
563	# SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for three callers: copilot-run (process env),
564	# `copilot-here on` (what it merges into settings.local.json) and
565	# Get-CopilotHereDrift (what it compares against). These used to be hand-maintained
566	# copies and they diverged — the drift check compared 4 of the 8 keys `on` writes,
567	# so a pin missing ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_HAIKU_MODEL / ANTHROPIC_SMALL_FAST_MODEL /
568	# CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC reported "no drift" while `on` would
569	# still have changed it. Add a key here and all three follow.
570	#
571	# -Pinned uses the shim base when the shim is enabled but not yet up (what a
572	# written-to-disk pin should say); copilot-run wants the live base instead.
573	function script:Get-CopilotEnvBlock {
574	    param([switch] $Pinned, [string] $Model = (Get-CopilotDefaultModel), $Catalog)
575	    $modelProfile = if ($PSBoundParameters.ContainsKey('Catalog')) {
576	        Get-CopilotModelProfile -Model $Model -Catalog $Catalog
577	    } else {
578	        Get-CopilotModelProfile -Model $Model
579	    }
580	    $block = [ordered]@{
581	        ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL             = if ($Pinned) { Get-CopilotPinnedBase } else { Get-CopilotClientBase }
582	        ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN           = 'dummy'
583	        ANTHROPIC_MODEL                = $modelProfile.main
584	        ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_FABLE_MODEL  = $modelProfile.fable
585	        ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_OPUS_MODEL   = $modelProfile.opus
586	        ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_SONNET_MODEL = $modelProfile.sonnet
587	        ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_HAIKU_MODEL  = $modelProfile.haiku
588	        ANTHROPIC_SMALL_FAST_MODEL     = $modelProfile.haiku
589	        CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC = '1'
590	    }
591	    if ($env:COPILOT_PROXY_QUIET -eq '1') {
592	        $block.CLAUDE_CODE_ATTRIBUTION_HEADER = '0'
593	        $block.CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_PROMPT_SUGGESTION = 'false'
594	        $block.CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_AWAY_SUMMARY = '0'
595	        $block.DISABLE_NON_ESSENTIAL_MODEL_CALLS = '1'
596	    }
597	    $block
598	}
