## Server-Side Tools: Advisor (Beta)

The advisor tool pairs a faster, lower-cost **executor** model (the top-level `model` on the request) with a higher-intelligence **advisor** model (the `model` field inside the tool definition) that provides strategic guidance mid-generation. The executor does most of the token generation; the advisor is consulted for planning. Availability: see `shared/platform-availability.md`.

### Tool Definition

```json
{
  "type": "advisor_20260301",
  "name": "advisor",
  "model": "claude-opus-4-8"
}
```

Optional fields on the tool definition:

- `max_uses` — cap on advisor consultations per request. Exceeding it makes the `advisor_tool_result` block's `content` the error object `{"type": "advisor_tool_result_error", "error_code": "max_uses_exceeded"}` — the third member of the content union in the payload-shape table below.
- `max_tokens` — bounds the advisor's total output (thinking + text) per call. At the cap the result block carries `stop_reason: "max_tokens"` and a truncation note is appended to the advice the executor sees; the server also emits a remaining-tokens budget block in the advisor's prompt so it self-shapes toward the cap.
- `caching` — cache-control for the advisor's own prompt, same shape as a cache breakpoint: `"caching": {"type": "ephemeral", "ttl": "5m"}` (`ttl` is `"5m"` or `"1h"`, default `"5m"`). Each call writes a cache entry at that TTL so later calls in the conversation read the stable prefix. Omitted = advisor prompt not cached.

**The advisor model must be at least as capable as the executor.** An invalid pairing returns `400 invalid_request_error`. Valid pairs:

| Executor (request `model`) | Valid advisor (tool `model`) |
|---|---|
| `claude-haiku-4-5` / `claude-sonnet-4-6` / `claude-sonnet-5` / `claude-opus-4-6` / `claude-opus-4-7` | `claude-opus-5`, `claude-fable-5`, `claude-mythos-5`, `claude-opus-4-8`, or `claude-opus-4-7` |
| `claude-opus-4-8` | `claude-opus-5`, `claude-fable-5`, `claude-mythos-5`, or `claude-opus-4-8` |
| `claude-opus-5` | `claude-opus-5`, `claude-fable-5`, or `claude-mythos-5` |
| `claude-fable-5` | `claude-fable-5` or `claude-opus-5` |
| `claude-mythos-5` | `claude-mythos-5` or `claude-opus-5` |

> ⚠️ **The advisor's payload shape differs by advisor model.** The response block is always `advisor_tool_result`; what varies is its **`content`**, a discriminated union:
>
> | `content` type | Fields | When |
> |---|---|---|
> | `advisor_result` | `text`, `stop_reason` | Advisor returns plaintext (e.g. Opus 4.8) |
> | `advisor_redacted_result` | `encrypted_content`, `stop_reason` | Advisor returns encrypted output — Claude Opus 5, Claude Fable 5, Claude Mythos 5 |
> | `advisor_tool_result_error` | `error_code` | Consultation failed — `max_uses_exceeded`, `prompt_too_long`, `too_many_requests`, `overloaded`, `unavailable`, `execution_time_exceeded`, or `model_not_found` |
>
> So switch on `advisor_tool_result.content` type, not on the block type. Code that reads `.text` unconditionally gets nothing back from an Claude Opus 5 advisor, because the payload is under `encrypted_content` instead — and you cannot read it, only replay it.

Call via `client.beta.messages.create(...)` with `betas=["advisor-tool-2026-03-01"]` (or the `anthropic-beta: advisor-tool-2026-03-01` header). In multi-turn conversations, append the full `response.content` — including any `advisor_tool_result` blocks — back to `messages` on the next turn. If you remove the advisor tool from `tools` on a later turn while the history still contains `advisor_tool_result` blocks, the API returns a 400.

> **Advisor on Managed Agents:** CMA sessions support an advisor too, configured as a `{"type": "advisor", "model"}` entry in the agent's multiagent roster rather than as a tool definition — no `max_uses`/`max_tokens`/`caching` options, and advice is delivered as thread events on the session's event stream rather than `advisor_tool_result` blocks. See `shared/managed-agents-multiagent.md` → Advisor.

---

## Client-Side Tools: Memory

The memory tool enables Claude to store and retrieve information across conversations through a memory file directory. Claude can create, read, update, and delete files that persist between sessions.

### Key Facts

- Client-side tool — you control storage via your implementation
- Supports commands: `view`, `create`, `str_replace`, `insert`, `delete`, `rename`
- Operates on files in a `/memories` directory
- The Python, TypeScript, and Java SDKs provide helper classes/functions for implementing the memory backend

> **Security:** Never store API keys, passwords, tokens, or other secrets in memory files. Be cautious with personally identifiable information (PII) — check data privacy regulations (GDPR, CCPA) before persisting user data. The reference implementations have no built-in access control; in multi-user systems, implement per-user memory directories and authentication in your tool handlers.

For full implementation examples, use WebFetch:

- Docs: `https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/memory-tool.md`

---

## Client-Side Tools: Bash and Text Editor

The bash and text editor tools are **Anthropic-defined, schema-less** tools. Declare them by `type` and `name` only — the input schema is built into the model and cannot be modified. **Do not pass an `input_schema`**, and do not define a custom tool that happens to be named `"bash"` — that creates a user-defined tool without the built-in behavior.

Both are **client-executed**: Claude returns a `tool_use` block, your code performs the action locally, and you send back a `tool_result`. The API is stateless; your application maintains the shell session or filesystem between turns.

### Bash tool declaration

```json
{"type": "bash_20250124", "name": "bash"}
```

| Language | Declaration |
|---|---|
| Python / TypeScript / Ruby / cURL | plain object `{"type": "bash_20250124", "name": "bash"}` |
| Go | `anthropic.ToolUnionParam{OfBashTool20250124: &anthropic.ToolBash20250124Param{}}` |
| Java | `.addTool(ToolBash20250124.builder().build())` from `com.anthropic.models.messages` |
| C# | `Tools = [new ToolBash20250124()]` from `Anthropic.Models.Messages` |
| PHP | `tools: [new \Anthropic\Messages\ToolBash20250124()]` |

Claude's `tool_use.input` contains either `{"command": "<string>"}` or `{"restart": true}`. Check for `restart` first (reset the session, return a confirmation string); otherwise run `command` and return combined stdout + stderr.

> **Security — commands are untrusted model output.** Run in an isolated environment (container, VM, or restricted user); apply an **allowlist** of permitted executables and reject shell operators (`&&`, `|`, `;`, `` ` ``, `$()`); set timeouts and resource limits; log every command. A blocklist is not sufficient.

### Text editor tool declaration

```json
{"type": "text_editor_20250728", "name": "str_replace_based_edit_tool"}
```

Optional field: `max_characters` to cap `view` output. Java exposes a typed `ToolTextEditor20250728` builder (`com.anthropic.models.messages`); other statically-typed SDKs follow the same naming pattern — see the Anthropic-Defined Tools section in `{lang}/claude-api/tool-use.md` for the exact class.

> **Security — `path` is untrusted model output. Confine every file operation to a fixed project root.** Before executing any command, resolve the model-supplied `path` to its canonical form and verify it remains within your project root; reject the request if it escapes (`..`, symlinks, absolute paths outside the root, URL-encoded traversal like `%2e%2e%2f`). Use your language's built-in path utilities (e.g., Python `pathlib.Path.resolve()` then check `.is_relative_to(root)`). Never call `open()` / `writeFile` / `unlink` directly on the raw `path` value.

`tool_use.input.command` is one of:

| `command` | Other inputs | Action |
|---|---|---|
| `view` | `path`, optional `view_range` | Return file contents or directory listing |
| `create` | `path`, `file_text` | Create/overwrite file with `file_text`. Create a backup if the file already exists. |
| `str_replace` | `path`, `old_str`, `new_str` | Replace exactly one occurrence; error if 0 or >1 matches |
| `insert` | `path`, `insert_line`, `insert_text` | Insert `insert_text` after line `insert_line` (0 = beginning of file) |

For both tools, on error return `{"type": "tool_result", "tool_use_id": "…", "content": "<error text>", "is_error": true}` so Claude can recover.

---

## Structured Outputs

Structured outputs constrain Claude's responses to follow a specific JSON schema, guaranteeing valid, parseable output. This is not a separate tool — it enhances the Messages API response format and/or tool parameter validation.

Two features are available:

- **JSON outputs** (`output_config.format`): Control Claude's response format
- **Strict tool use** (`strict: true`): Guarantee valid tool parameter schemas

**Supported models:** Claude Fable 5, Claude Opus 5, Claude Opus 4.8, Claude Sonnet 5, and Claude Haiku 4.5. Legacy models (Claude Opus 4.5, Claude Opus 4.1) also support structured outputs.

> **Recommended:** Use `client.messages.parse()` which automatically validates responses against your schema. When using `messages.create()` directly, use `output_config: {format: {...}}`. The `output_format` convenience parameter is also accepted by some SDK methods (e.g., `.parse()`), but `output_config.format` is the canonical API-level parameter.

### JSON Schema Limitations

**Supported:**

- Basic types: object, array, string, integer, number, boolean, null
- `enum`, `const`, `anyOf`, `allOf`, `$ref`/`$def`
- String formats: `date-time`, `time`, `date`, `duration`, `email`, `hostname`, `uri`, `ipv4`, `ipv6`, `uuid`
- `additionalProperties: false` (required for all objects)

**Not supported:**

- Recursive schemas
- Numerical constraints (`minimum`, `maximum`, `multipleOf`)
- String constraints (`minLength`, `maxLength`)
- Complex array constraints
- `additionalProperties` set to anything other than `false`

The Python and TypeScript SDKs automatically handle unsupported constraints by removing them from the schema sent to the API and validating them client-side.

### Important Notes

- **First request latency**: New schemas incur a one-time compilation cost. Subsequent requests with the same schema use a 24-hour cache.
- **Refusals**: If Claude refuses for safety reasons (`stop_reason: "refusal"`), the output may not match your schema.
- **Token limits**: If `stop_reason: "max_tokens"`, output may be incomplete. Increase `max_tokens`.
- **Incompatible with**: Citations (returns 400 error), message prefilling.
- **Works with**: Batches API, streaming, token counting, extended thinking.

---

## Tips for Effective Tool Use

1. **Provide detailed descriptions**: Claude relies heavily on descriptions to understand when and how to use tools
2. **Use specific tool names**: `get_current_weather` is better than `weather`
3. **Validate inputs**: Always validate tool inputs before execution
4. **Handle errors gracefully**: Return informative error messages so Claude can adapt
5. **Limit tool count**: Too many tools can confuse the model — keep the set focused
6. **Test tool interactions**: Verify Claude uses tools correctly in various scenarios

For detailed tool use documentation, use WebFetch:

- URL: `https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/overview`
</doc>

## When to Use WebFetch

Use WebFetch to get the latest documentation when:

- User asks for "latest" or "current" information
- Cached data seems incorrect
- User asks about features not covered here

Live documentation URLs are in `shared/live-sources.md`.

## Common Pitfalls

- Don't truncate inputs when passing files or content to the API. If the content is too long to fit in the context window, notify the user and discuss options (chunking, summarization, etc.) rather than silently truncating.
- **Prefill removed (Fable 5, Opus 5, Sonnet 5, and the 4.6/4.7/4.8 family):** Assistant message prefills (last-assistant-turn prefills) return a 400 error on Fable 5, Opus 5, Sonnet 5, Opus 4.6, Opus 4.7, Opus 4.8, and Sonnet 4.6. Use structured outputs (`output_config.format`) or system prompt instructions to control response format instead. (One exception: the fallback-credit prefill claim — when redeeming a credit with `fallback_has_prefill_claim: true`, the server accepts the echoed assistant message; see the migration guide's refusal section.)
- **Confirm migration scope before editing:** When a user asks to migrate code to a newer Claude model without naming a specific file, directory, or file list, **ask which scope to apply first** — the entire working directory, a specific subdirectory, or a specific set of files. Do not start editing until the user confirms. Imperative phrasings like "migrate my codebase", "move my project to X", "upgrade to Sonnet 4.6", or bare "migrate to Opus 4.8" are **still ambiguous** — they tell you what to do but not where, so ask. Proceed without asking only when the prompt names an exact file, a specific directory, or an explicit file list ("migrate `app.py`", "migrate everything under `services/`", "update `a.py` and `b.py`"). See `shared/model-migration.md` Step 0.
- **`max_tokens` defaults:** Don't lowball `max_tokens` — hitting the cap truncates output mid-thought and requires a retry. For non-streaming requests, default to `~16000` (keeps responses under SDK HTTP timeouts). For streaming requests, default to `~64000` (timeouts aren't a concern, so give the model room). Only go lower when you have a hard reason: classification (`~256`), cost caps, deliberately short outputs, or **`max_tokens: 0`** for cache pre-warming (see `shared/prompt-caching.md` → Pre-warming).
- **Disabling thinking on Claude Opus 5 has two failure modes — prefer low/medium effort instead.** Only affects code that explicitly opts out; thinking is on by default, so watch for a disabled-thinking setting carried forward from Opus 4.8. With `thinking: {type: "disabled"}`, the model occasionally writes a tool call into its **visible text** instead of a `tool_use` block: the turn succeeds, the call never runs, no error is raised, and in an agentic loop that text pollutes later turns. It can also leak `<thinking>` tags into the response. Turning thinking on and lowering `effort` fixes both and still cuts cost. If a route must stay thinking-off: add *"You may say a brief sentence before using a tool"*, **delete** any don't-think/don't-reason rule (it makes tag leakage worse), and use a generic *"Do not include internal or system XML tags in your response"* rather than naming thinking tags. Details: `shared/model-migration.md` → Two failure modes when thinking is disabled.
- **128K output tokens:** Fable 5, Opus 5, Opus 4.6, Opus 4.7, Opus 4.8, Sonnet 5, and Sonnet 4.6 support up to 128K `max_tokens`, but the SDKs require streaming for values that large to avoid HTTP timeouts. Use `.stream()` with `.get_final_message()` / `.finalMessage()`.
- **Tool call JSON parsing (Fable 5, Opus 5, and the 4.6/4.7/4.8 family):** Fable 5, Opus 5, Opus 4.6, Opus 4.7, Opus 4.8, and Sonnet 4.6 may produce different JSON string escaping in tool call `input` fields (e.g., Unicode or forward-slash escaping). Always parse tool inputs with `json.loads()` / `JSON.parse()` — never do raw string matching on the serialized input.
- **Structured outputs (all models):** Use `output_config: {format: {...}}` instead of the deprecated `output_format` parameter on `messages.create()`. This is a general API change, not 4.6-specific.
- **Don't reimplement SDK functionality:** The SDK provides high-level helpers — use them instead of building from scratch. Specifically: use `stream.finalMessage()` instead of wrapping `.on()` events in `new Promise()`; use typed exception classes (`Anthropic.RateLimitError`, etc.) instead of string-matching error messages; use SDK types (`Anthropic.MessageParam`, `Anthropic.Tool`, `Anthropic.Message`, etc.) instead of redefining equivalent interfaces.
- **Error handling — catch a chain, not one broad class.** A single `except APIStatusError` / `catch (AnthropicServiceException)` / `rescue APIError` loses the distinction between retryable (429, ≥500, network) and non-retryable (400/404) failures. Write a most-specific-first chain — e.g. `NotFoundError` → `RateLimitError` → `APIStatusError` → `APIConnectionError` (or the Go equivalent: `errors.As` into `*anthropic.Error` then `switch apierr.StatusCode { case 404: …; case 429: …; default: … }`). Per-language class names and namespaces are in `shared/error-codes.md`.
- **Don't research SDK types — write first.** If a type name isn't shown in the documentation included in this skill, write the code file from the namespace/package tables in the language-specific doc and let the compiler's error point you to the right name. Do not spend turns on WebFetch, SDK-repo clones, or compiling-and-running a separate reflection program to discover type names before writing — produce the source file first, then fix what the compiler reports. A quick `strings` / `jar tf` / `javap` against the installed SDK is acceptable for locating names (it returns in seconds), but don't escalate beyond that. A file with a wrong type name is recoverable; a session spent on discovery with no file written is not.
- **Bash and text editor tools are Anthropic-defined, schema-less.** Declare `{"type": "bash_20250124", "name": "bash"}` / `{"type": "text_editor_20250728", "name": "str_replace_based_edit_tool"}` — no `input_schema`. A custom tool with your own schema named `"bash"` is a different tool. Handler paths and security checks are in `shared/tool-use-concepts.md` § Client-Side Tools.
- **Advisor tool model pairing.** The advisor tool's `model` must be at least as capable as the request's top-level `model` — e.g. executor `claude-sonnet-5` → advisor `claude-opus-4-8` or `claude-opus-4-7`. An invalid pair returns 400. Pairing table in `shared/tool-use-concepts.md` § Advisor. Availability: `shared/platform-availability.md`.
- **Agent Skills ≠ Managed Agents.** To have Claude generate a `.pptx`/`.xlsx`/etc. via Agent Skills, call `client.beta.messages.create` with `container={"skills": [...]}`, the `code_execution_20260521` tool, and both `code-execution-2025-08-25` + `skills-2025-10-02` betas. Do not use `client.beta.agents` / `sessions` / `environments` here — those are the Managed Agents surface, not Agent Skills.
- **MCP connector needs both halves.** `mcp_servers=[{type:"url", url, name}]` alone is rejected as a validation error — also add `tools=[{type:"mcp_toolset", mcp_server_name:<same name>}]` with beta `mcp-client-2025-11-20`. Availability: `shared/platform-availability.md`.
- **`inference_geo` is a direct top-level request parameter** — `client.messages.create(..., inference_geo="us")` / `.inferenceGeo("us")`. Do not put it in `extra_body` / `putAdditionalBodyProperty`. (Messages API only — on Managed Agents, `inference_geo` instead nests inside the agent's `model` object, never top-level; see `shared/managed-agents-core.md` § Pinning inference geography.) Supported on Opus 4.6 / Sonnet 4.6 and later; availability: `shared/platform-availability.md`. `response.usage.inference_geo` reports where inference ran.
- **Fine-grained tool streaming is not a beta feature.** Set `eager_input_streaming: true` on the tool definition and call the regular `client.messages.stream(...)`. There is no beta header and no `client.beta.*` path.
- **Cache diagnostics is beta.** Use `client.beta.messages.*` with beta `cache-diagnosis-2026-04-07`. Pass `diagnostics: {previous_message_id: null}` on the first turn and `diagnostics: {previous_message_id: <previous response id>}` on subsequent turns; the result is on `response.diagnostics`. Availability: `shared/platform-availability.md`.
- **Memory tool type is `memory_20250818`.** Declare `{"type": "memory_20250818", "name": "memory"}`. Go uses the beta-namespace type `{OfMemoryTool20250818: &anthropic.BetaMemoryTool20250818Param{}}` on `client.Beta.Messages.New`; Python/TypeScript/Ruby/PHP/C# use the non-beta `client.messages.create`; Java has both a non-beta `MemoryTool20250818` and a beta tool-runner path. Python/TypeScript provide `BetaAbstractMemoryTool` / `betaMemoryTool` helpers for implementing the backend.
- **Use a model the feature actually supports.** Some features are restricted to specific model tiers — fast mode is Claude Opus 5 / Opus 4.8 only (and Claude API only), task budgets (Messages API only — Managed Agents session budgets have no model-tier restriction) are Claude Opus 5 / Fable 5 / Sonnet 5 / Opus 4.8 / 4.7 only, and the advisor tool requires a valid executor↔advisor pair. If the user's prompt names a model that the feature doesn't support, use a supported model instead and note the substitution in the output.
- **Don't define custom types for SDK data structures:** The SDK exports types for all API objects. Use `Anthropic.MessageParam` for messages, `Anthropic.Tool` for tool definitions, `Anthropic.ToolUseBlock` / `Anthropic.ToolResultBlockParam` for tool results, `Anthropic.Message` for responses. Defining your own `interface ChatMessage { role: string; content: unknown }` duplicates what the SDK already provides and loses type safety.
- **Report and document output:** For tasks that produce reports, documents, or visualizations, the code execution sandbox has `python-docx`, `python-pptx`, `matplotlib`, `pillow`, and `pypdf` pre-installed. Claude can generate formatted files (DOCX, PDF, charts) and return them via the Files API — consider this for "report" or "document" type requests instead of plain stdout text.
- **Server-tool errors don't raise.** Web search and web fetch errors return HTTP 200 with a `web_search_tool_result` / `web_fetch_tool_result` block whose `content` is a single error object (e.g. `{error_code: "max_uses_exceeded"}`) — not a raised exception. For web search, a success `content` is a *list*; an error `content` is an *object* — branch on that before indexing.
- **Code execution output block type:** `code_execution_20260521` returns `bash_code_execution_tool_result` (with `.content.stdout`), **not** the legacy bare `code_execution_tool_result`. Iterate `response.content` and match on the correct type.
- **Tool search: never defer everything.** The search tool itself must not have `defer_loading: true`, and at least one tool in `tools` must be non-deferred, or the API returns 400 `All tools have defer_loading set`.

256	            -WorkingDirectory $Dir -PassThru -NoNewWindow -ErrorAction Stop

```text
1	# `modify_config.toml: invalid TOML ... Empty key at line 1 col 0`
2	
3	**Symptoms** (grep this section): `chezmoi update --init` or `chezmoi apply`
4	prints:
5	
6	```text
7	modify_config.toml: invalid TOML; preserving live config unchanged: Empty key at line 1 col 0
8	```
9	
10	The existing `~/.codex/config.toml` looks empty or valid in an editor, and the
11	managed `tui.status_line` is not applied.
12	**First seen**: 2026-08
13	**Affects**: Windows dotfiles at the first `modify_`-based Codex footer release,
14	when the live config starts with a UTF-8 BOM.
15	**Status**: fixed — the modifier accepts one BOM and preserves every failure path
16	byte-for-byte.
17	
18	## Symptom
19	
20	The parser reports an empty key at the very first column even though line 1 does
21	not contain an empty TOML assignment. Missing and ordinary zero-byte files work;
22	an existing file created by a Windows editor can fail.
23	
24	A separate CI symptom had the same outward result (the old status line survived):
25	Python existed on `windows-latest`, but `tomlkit` did not. The old Pester helper
26	discarded stderr, so the import failure was hidden.
27	
28	## Root cause
29	
30	The first implementation read stdin through `[Console]::In.ReadToEnd()`.
31	`Console.In` decoded the leading UTF-8 BOM into the literal character U+FEFF;
32	`[string]::IsNullOrWhiteSpace([char]0xFEFF)` is false, so the fresh-input shortcut
33	did not run. The parsing copy still began with U+FEFF. TOML permits space, tab,
34	LF, and CRLF as whitespace, not U+FEFF, so `tomlkit` attempted to parse a key,
35	consumed zero valid key characters, and raised `Empty key at line 1 col 0`.
36	
37	The same text-mode path also made “preserving unchanged” weaker than advertised:
38	invalid UTF-8 could be replaced during decode, and Python universal-newline reads
39	could turn CRLF into LF.
40	
41	References:
42	
43	- [TOML 1.0 whitespace and newline grammar](https://toml.io/en/v1.0.0)
44	- [.NET `Console` implementation](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/v8.0.0/src/libraries/System.Console/src/System/ConsolePal.Windows.cs)
45	- [`tomlkit` parser](https://github.com/python-poetry/tomlkit/blob/0.13.3/tomlkit/parser.py)
46	
47	## Workaround
48	
49	Apply the fixed modifier. It reads stdin as bytes, strips exactly one BOM only
50	from the parsing copy, and emits successful output as UTF-8 without BOM:
51	
52	```powershell
53	chezmoi apply ~/.codex/config.toml
54	```
55	
56	Before the fix, remove one BOM only after backing up the file:
57	
58	```powershell
59	$p = Join-Path $HOME '.codex/config.toml'
60	Copy-Item $p "$p.bak"
61	$text = [IO.File]::ReadAllText($p)
62	if ($text.Length -gt 0 -and $text[0] -eq [char]0xFEFF) {
63	    [IO.File]::WriteAllText($p, $text.Substring(1), [Text.UTF8Encoding]::new($false))
64	}
65	chezmoi apply $p
66	```
67	
68	Do not replace or truncate a nonblank file merely because parsing failed; it may
69	contain providers, project trust, plugins, or credentials that the overlay must
70	preserve.
71	
72	## Prevention
73	
74	- Treat a `modify_` target as a byte stream until parsing succeeds.
75	- Decode with strict UTF-8 and retain the original bytes for every fail-closed
76	  return.
77	- Accept at most one leading BOM; do not use `.IsNullOrWhiteSpace()` as TOML’s
78	  whitespace grammar.
79	- Capture stderr and assert bytes in Pester. Include BOM-only, BOM-prefixed valid
80	  TOML, malformed CRLF, invalid UTF-8, double-BOM, and idempotence cases.
81	- Provision the same pinned parser runtime in CI and seed a non-empty target before
82	  `chezmoi apply`; an empty target does not exercise the merge path.
83	
84	## Related
85	
86	- [`docs/codex-status-line.md`](../docs/codex-status-line.md)
87	- [`dot_codex/modify_config.toml.ps1.tmpl`](../dot_codex/modify_config.toml.ps1.tmpl)
88	- [`tests/CodexConfig.Tests.ps1`](../tests/CodexConfig.Tests.ps1)
89

<summary>Tool use: **Read**</summary>
 `./pitfalls/copilot-proxy-npm-etarget-but-doctor-says-installed.md`

```text
1	# `npm ETARGET` is followed by `copilot-proxy doctor` saying the requested version is installed
2	
3	**Symptoms** (grep this section): `copilot-proxy restart` prints:
4	
5	```text
6	copilot-proxy: installing @jeffreycao/copilot-api@2.1.0 (one-time — later starts skip this) ...
7	npm error code ETARGET
8	npm error notarget No matching version found for @jeffreycao/copilot-api@2.1.0.
9	copilot-proxy: starting (@jeffreycao/copilot-api@2.1.0) on port 4141 ...
10	```
11	
12	A subsequent doctor contradicts npm:
13	
14	```text
15	Package
16	  ✓ installed        @jeffreycao/copilot-api@2.1.0
17	```
18	
19	The proxy can listen and serve models because it actually launched an older tree
20	left in `~/.local/share/copilot-api/pkg`.
21	**First seen**: 2026-08
22	**Affects**: the Windows Copilot module before installed `package.json` metadata
23	became the installation postcondition, especially after the pin changed from
24	`1.13.14` to `2.1.0` on a lagging corporate npm mirror.
25	**Status**: fixed — stale package contents cannot satisfy readiness or receive a
26	new stamp.
27	
28	## Root cause
29	
30	The old installer used this success test after npm/Bun exited:
31	
32	1. any `node_modules/.bin/copilot-api*` shim exists, **or**
33	2. any `node_modules/@jeffreycao/copilot-api` directory exists.
34	
35	It did not read that package’s `package.json`. When npm returned `ETARGET`, the
36	old package tree remained, the weak filesystem predicate returned true, and the
37	installer wrote the **requested string** `@jeffreycao/copilot-api@2.1.0` to
38	`.installed-spec`. Doctor trusted that stamp plus the same old directory/binlink,
39	so it claimed 2.1.0 and `start` launched the stale binary.
40	
41	The exact 2.1.0 release exists on public npm. In the first report, `ETARGET` was
42	therefore consistent with the configured corporate pull-through mirror not having
43	synchronized that version yet—not evidence that the public package never existed.
44	
45	Reference: [public npm metadata for 2.1.0](https://registry.npmjs.org/@jeffreycao%2Fcopilot-api/2.1.0).
46	
47	## Workaround
48	
49	First identify the registry and verify the exact pin **before** deleting the
50	working prefix:
51	
52	```powershell
53	npm config get registry
54	npm view '@jeffreycao/copilot-api@2.1.0' version
55	# Compare only where direct public npm is permitted:
56	npm view '@jeffreycao/copilot-api@2.1.0' version --registry https://registry.npmjs.org/
57	```
58	
59	If only the corporate mirror is missing 2.1.0, wait/request synchronization or
60	use an approved registry for the reinstall. Then deploy the fixed module and
61	reinstall:
62	
63	```powershell
64	chezmoi apply ~/.config/powershell/modules/Copilot/Copilot.psm1
65	copilot-proxy reinstall
66	copilot-proxy doctor
67	```
68	
69	Do not switch the managed pin to `latest`; that trades a diagnosable mirror delay
70	for an unreviewed gateway upgrade.
71	
72	## Prevention
73	
74	- Read installed `package.json.name` and `.version`; a directory or binlink is not
75	  proof of which package landed.
76	- Store requested spec plus verified installed name/version in the stamp, and
77	  compare the stamp back to live metadata on every readiness check.
78	- Write the stamp only after metadata and a runnable launch path agree.
79	- Keep filesystem metadata as the authoritative postcondition. The existing
80	  Windows `Start-Process` child shape has returned misleading exit-code data, so
81	  exit status alone is insufficient.
82	- Test the exact regression: stale 1.13.14 tree + desired 2.1.0 + failed installer
83	  must return false, write no 2.1.0 stamp, and never reach proxy launch.
84	
85	## Related
86	
87	- [`copilot-api-connectionrefused-stale-bun-only-module`](copilot-api-connectionrefused-stale-bun-only-module.md)
88	- [`packagefeedproxy-npm-404-wrong-base-path`](packagefeedproxy-npm-404-wrong-base-path.md)
89	- [`docs/copilot-proxy.md`](../docs/copilot-proxy.md)
90

827	# --- shim start/stop ---
828	function script:Start-CopilotShim {

830	    if (-not (Get-Command bun -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue)) {
831	        Write-Error "copilot-proxy: shim needs 'bun' (scoop install bun)"; return $false
832	    }
833	    $script = Get-CopilotShimScript
834	    if (-not (Test-Path $script)) { Write-Error "copilot-proxy: shim script not found at $script"; return $false }
835	    $env:COPILOT_SHIM_PORT = Get-CopilotShimPort
836	    $env:COPILOT_SHIM_UPSTREAM = Get-CopilotBase
837	    $p = Start-Process -FilePath 'bun' -ArgumentList @($script) -PassThru -WindowStyle Hidden `
838	        -RedirectStandardOutput (Get-CopilotShimLog) -RedirectStandardError "$(Get-CopilotShimLog).err"
839	    $p.Id | Set-Content -Path (Get-CopilotShimPid)
840	    for ($i = 0; $i -lt 10; $i++) { if (Test-CopilotShimAlive) { return $true }; Start-Sleep 1 }
841	    Write-Error "copilot-proxy: shim did not come up — check $(Get-CopilotShimLog)"; $false
842	}
843	function script:Stop-CopilotShim {
844	    $pidf = Get-CopilotShimPid
845	    if (Test-Path $pidf) {
846	        $pid_ = Get-Content -First 1 $pidf -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
847	        if ($pid_) { Stop-Process -Id $pid_ -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue }
848	        Remove-Item $pidf -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
849	    }
850	    Get-CimInstance Win32_Process -Filter "Name = 'bun.exe'" -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue |
851	        Where-Object { $_.CommandLine -like '*copilot-throttle-shim.js*' } |
852	        ForEach-Object { Stop-Process -Id $_.ProcessId -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue }
853	}
854	
855	# ============================================================ copilot-proxy ===
856	function copilot-proxy {
857	    [CmdletBinding()]
858	    param([Parameter(ValueFromRemainingArguments)] [string[]] $Argv)
859	
860	    if (-not (Get-Command bun -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue)) {
861	        Write-Error "copilot-proxy: bun not found (scoop install bun)"; return
862	    }
863	
864	    $port = Get-CopilotPort; $pkg = Get-CopilotPkg
865	    $logf = Get-CopilotLogFile; $pidf = Get-CopilotPidFile
866	    $action = if ($Argv -and $Argv.Count -ge 1) { $Argv[0] } else { 'status' }
867	
868	    switch ($action) {
869	        'start' {
870	            if (Test-CopilotAlive) { Write-Host "copilot-proxy: already running on port $port"; return }
871	            if (-not (Test-Path (Get-CopilotToken))) {
872	                Write-Error "copilot-proxy: not authenticated yet — run 'copilot-proxy auth' first."; return
873	            }
874	            # Rotate the previous session's log (keep last 3).
875	            if (Test-Path $logf) {
876	                Remove-Item "$logf.3" -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
877	                if (Test-Path "$logf.2") { Move-Item -Force "$logf.2" "$logf.3" }
878	                if (Test-Path "$logf.1") { Move-Item -Force "$logf.1" "$logf.2" }
879	                Move-Item -Force $logf "$logf.1"
880	            }
881	            # Install the pinned package BEFORE launching anything. Resolving it at
882	            # launch (the old `bunx <pkg> start`) is what used to hang forever behind
883	            # a socks proxy, with nothing but "Resolving dependencies" in the log.
884	            if (-not (Install-CopilotPkg)) { return }
885	            $launch = Get-CopilotPkgLaunch
886	            if (-not $launch) { Write-Error "copilot-proxy: no runnable copilot-api after install"; return }
887	
888	            # Node ignores the Windows System Proxy — it only honours HTTP(S)_PROXY,
889	            # and the fork additionally needs --proxy-env before its fetch uses them.
890	            $httpProxy = Resolve-CopilotHttpProxy
891	            if ($httpProxy) {
892	                Write-Host "copilot-proxy: Node will fetch /models via $httpProxy (--proxy-env; COPILOT_HTTP_PROXY=$(if ($env:COPILOT_HTTP_PROXY) { $env:COPILOT_HTTP_PROXY } else { 'auto' }))"
893	            } elseif ($env:COPILOT_HTTP_PROXY -in 'always', 'on', '1', 'true', 'yes') {
894	                Write-Warning "copilot-proxy: COPILOT_HTTP_PROXY=always but no proxy detected — starting DIRECT (the Claude catalog may be geo-filtered)."
895	                Write-Host "  hint: enable the Clash/Verge System Proxy, or set COPILOT_HTTP_PROXY=http://127.0.0.1:7897"
896	            }

# chezmoi-dotfiles

This machine's `$HOME` is managed by a **chezmoi** (configs) + **ansible** (system
deps) dotfiles repo. This skill is the agent-facing map: how to drive it, and what
custom tooling exists that you wouldn't otherwise know about. It is rendered per-host
— the "What's enabled on THIS machine" section reflects what the user actually
selected at init.

## Orientation (read this first)

- **Repo root**: `chezmoi source-path` (no args) prints the source dir. Work there
  to edit: `cd "$(chezmoi source-path)"`.
- **Source path of one file**: `chezmoi source-path ~/.config/foo/bar` → the
  managed source file for that target.
- **`docs/**` is NOT deployed to `$HOME`** (it's chezmoi-ignored). Read detail via
  `"$(chezmoi source-path)/docs/..."`. A *subset* is deployed to `~/.config/docs/`
  (e.g. keybindings, cli-tools) for runtime helpers.
- **Read the contract before editing**: `"$(chezmoi source-path)/CLAUDE.md"` holds
  Hard invariants and cross-file maintenance rules. Honor them.
- This host: profile `macos`, OS `darwin`/`amd64`, primary shell `zsh`.

## chezmoi essentials

```bash
chezmoi diff                 # preview changes (also: just chezmoi-diff)
chezmoi apply                # deploy + run scripts (also: cas, or just chezmoi-apply)
chezmoi status               # modified/added/removed targets
chezmoi edit ~/.zshrc        # edit the SOURCE of a target
chezmoi add  ~/.config/x     # start managing an existing file
chezmoi re-add               # pull live edits back into source
chezmoi managed | grep foo   # is X managed?
chezmoi cat ~/.config/x      # render a target without applying
chezmoi data | jq            # the template data (ground truth for the toggles below)
```

- **`cas`** = `chezmoi apply` + reload hint; **`cau`** = update from remote then apply
  (defined in `dot_config/shell/99_chezmoi_reload.sh`).
- **`dotcfg`** = reconfigure the init prompts on an already-set-up machine
  (`dotcfg` for the TUI, `dotcfg --set installLlmTools=true --yes` for one toggle,
  `dotcfg --dry-run` to preview). Shell twin: `czcfg`.
- **Never `chezmoi add` a `modify_`/`create_` target** — it overwrites the script.
- Full command cheat-sheet: `docs/this_repo/cheatsheet.md`. Install-vs-upgrade is
  split: `chezmoi apply`/ansible is **install-only**; upgrades go through
  `just upgrade-*`.

## What's enabled on THIS machine

(Rendered from this host's selections. For live truth: `chezmoi data | jq`.)
- **Coding agents** — Claude Code, OpenCode, Cursor, Codex, Gemini, Copilot (configs + CLIs). See `docs/tools/agent-overlays.md`, `docs/tools/agent-skills.md`.
- **Python uv tools** — mlflow, marimo, jupyter, etc. (powers the `mlf` CLI). See `docs/this_repo/uv-bootstrap.md`.
- **Extra runtimes** — rust, bun, ruby via mise (+ cargo/gem tools). Node is always present.
- **LLM tools** — Ollama / LiteLLM / local models.
- **JS CLI tools** — standalone npm CLIs (e.g. readability-cli).
- **.NET tools** — .NET SDK (mise) + dotnet global tools.
- **IaC** — Azure CLI, Terraform, OpenTofu.
- **Media** — ffmpeg, ImageMagick, exiftool, libvips.
- **Media control** — nowplaying-cli + switchaudio-osx (macOS) / playerctl (Linux); unlocks full `sysplay`/`sysnow` (built-in `sysvol`/`sysmute` work regardless).
- **Networking** — nmap, mtr, httpie, gping, trippy.
- **Tunnels** — ngrok, cloudflared (expose localhost to the **public** internet).
- **Tailscale** — WireGuard mesh VPN (tailnet-only, the opposite of the tunnel tools). Helper CLI: `tsnet`. Picker: `tv tailnet`. See `docs/tools/tsnet.md`, `docs/tools/Tailscale.md`.
- **Agent sounds** — audio notifications on agent Stop/Notification hooks. See `docs/tools/agent-sounds.md`.
- **Vim mode** — shell modal editing + tmux vim nav (NOT Neovim/editors — those are always vim).

## Custom in-house CLIs (always deployed to `~/.dotfiles/bin`, on PATH)

Each works from any cwd. Run with `--help`. Most have `docs/tools/<name>.md`, but not all (`x` → `clipboard.md`, `view-ebook` → `yazi-previews.md`, `fleet` → `this_repo/fleet-apply.md`); grep `docs/` if the obvious path 404s. Full list: `ls "$(chezmoi source-path)/dot_dotfiles/bin/"`.

- **`fleet`** — cross-host ops over your machines: `fleet chezmoi apply`, `fleet hosts`, `fleet tmux`, `fleet info`, `fleet pueue`, `fleet exec`. See `docs/this_repo/fleet-apply.md`, `docs/tools/fleet-exec.md`, `docs/tools/fleet-hosts.md`.
- **`mlf`** — MLflow umbrella CLI + TUI dashboard (needs Python uv tools). Picker twin: `tv mlflow`.
- **`pqsum`** — pueue queue summary (text / AI / JSON). See `docs/tools/pueue.md`.
- **`x`** — clipboard/file copy-paste-open with cross-platform fallbacks.
- **`view-office`** / **`view-ebook`** — open/preview Office docs (.docx/.xlsx/.pptx + legacy .doc/.xls/.ppt) and ebooks (epub/mobi/azw3, calibre-backed) in the terminal; also power the yazi previewers. See `docs/tools/office-viewers.md`, `docs/tools/yazi-previews.md`.
- **`mi-router`** / **`reyee`** / **`sms`** — read-only router CLIs (Xiaomi MiWiFi / Ruijie Reyee / Huawei HiLink SMS). See `docs/tools/{mi-router,reyee,sms}.md`.
- **`mi-dhcp-bind`** — opt-in **write** companion to `mi-router`: set/remove MiWiFi static DHCP reservations (`bind --self` autodetects this host). See `docs/tools/mi-dhcp-bind.md`.
- **`ping-monitor`** — record ping over time, flag latency spikes. See `docs/tools/ping-monitor.md`.
- **`wake`** — Wake-on-LAN sender: `wake <host>` powers a box on by magic packet (hosts in `~/.config/wake/hosts.toml`). Passive side = `installWakeOnLan` ansible role. See `docs/sysadmin/wake-on-lan.md`.
- **`tsnet`** — Tailscale helper: `tsnet list` (tailnet devices, `--tsv`/`--json`), `tsnet ssh-config <machine>` (idempotent managed block in `~/.ssh/config.d/20-tailscale`; detects the legacy no-`Include` case and shadowing `Host` blocks, both of which make ssh config silently inert), `tsnet serve <port>` (preflight → `tailscale serve --bg --https=443` → verify, for services that hard-require an `https://` origin), `tsnet doctor`. `--host H` drives any of it on a remote box over ssh. Picker twin: `tv tailnet`. See `docs/tools/tsnet.md`.
- **`agent-warmup`** — drive a real interactive agent TUI at a scheduled time to move the quota window (launchd/systemd/pueue). See `docs/tools/agent-warmup.md`.
- **`crash-blackbox`** — flight recorder for hard power-offs / unclean shutdowns. See `docs/tools/crash-blackbox.md`.
- **`nvidia-driver-drift-check`** — flag kernel-module vs userspace driver drift. See `docs/sysadmin/gpu-driver.md`.
- **`yth`** — search your YouTube watch history (title/channel/description + captions; Takeout import + optional cookie sync). Picker twin: `tv yth`. See `docs/tools/yth.md`.
- **`appsrc`** — detect how an installed app / CLI was installed & managed (cask / App Store / direct-download / apt / snap / flatpak / AppImage / cargo/npm/pipx/uv/mise/go/gem / manual): `appsrc which <cmd-or-app>` (live), `appsrc size <app>` (footprint + associated cache/data/containers), `appsrc tui` (interactive dashboard — sort by size, filter), bare `appsrc` / `appsrc scan` (cached inventory, `--json`/`--tsv`/`--size`/`--sort`). Picker twins: `tv appsrc` (by source) / `tv appsrc-size` (by footprint). See `docs/tools/appsrc.md`.
- **`herdr-grep`** — search visible or retained content across panes in the current, one named, or all running local Herdr sessions; reports exact session/workspace/tab/pane coordinates, supports `--json`, and `--pick` pipes matches to fzf then exact-focuses/attaches the selection. Inside Herdr, `prefix+Alt+F` opens a visible-content picker (Alt+S = scrollback, Alt+V = visible). Remote use runs the CLI through SSH. See `docs/tools/herdr.md`.
- **`dotcfg`** — reconfigure dotfiles prompts (above).
- **`sesh-preview`** — preview helper for the sesh picker.

**`herdr`** is a first-class managed surface too (config in `dot_config/herdr/`, upgrade via `just upgrade-herdr` — which must NOT be run from inside a herdr pane): a remote pane/workspace server with three metadata pickers (`tv herdr-agent-panes`, `tv herdr-review`, `tv herdr-sesh`) plus `herdr-grep` for pane-content search. See `docs/tools/herdr.md` and the herdr entries in `pitfalls/`. Distinct from `wt` (worktrunk) and `wm` (workmux).

## Television (`tv`) — fuzzy pickers with custom channels

There are ~50 **custom** channels (system state, fleet, services, infra, agents…)
that you won't discover otherwise. Browse them:

```bash
tv                      # default picker
tv list-channels        # list everything available
tv <channel>            # open one, e.g. tv fleet-hosts | tv mlflow | tv pueue
ls "$(chezmoi source-path)/dot_config/television/cable/"   # the channel definitions
```

Handy ones: `fleet-hosts`, `tailnet`, `ssh-config`, `mlflow`, `pueue`, `ports`,
`kill-process`, `services`, `sessions`, `keybindings`, `aliases`, `git-ops`,
`mac-apps`/`linux-apps`, the agent trio (`agent-panes`, `agent-sessions`,
`agent-wakeup`) and the `herdr-*` family. Full reference: `docs/tools/tv.md`.

## Keybindings & keymaps

- **`bindings`** (shell function) or **`tv keybindings`** — interactive reference.
- **tmux**: `prefix + Space` opens the action menu. There is **no `prefix + e`** —
  that alias was removed, and `prefix + E` is "break every pane into its own
  window", so do not guess it. `prefix + T` = sesh picker, `prefix + U` = tools.
  Deep ref: `docs/tools/tmux/keybindings.md`.
- **shell ZLE widgets**: `Alt+S` sesh sessions, `Alt+T` tools, `Ctrl+R` history (atuin).
- Master reference: `docs/shells/keybindings.md` (also deployed to `~/.config/docs/shells/keybindings.md`).

## Aliases & functions

`alias` to list shell aliases, or `tv aliases`. Catalog: `docs/shells/aliases.md`.
Helpers worth knowing: `chezmoi-cd` (jump to source), `run-for` (time-box a command),

#!/usr/bin/env pwsh
# chezmoi modify_ script: enforce only Codex's native footer while preserving
# every unrelated live setting (providers, projects, plugins, feature flags).
# Runs under [interpreters.ps1]. A malformed live file is passed through
# unchanged: config recovery must be explicit, never an accidental overwrite.

$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'

function Write-StdoutBytes {
    param([byte[]] $Bytes)
    $out = [Console]::OpenStandardOutput()
    $out.Write($Bytes, 0, $Bytes.Length)
    $out.Flush()
}

$utf8 = [System.Text.UTF8Encoding]::new($false)
$overlayText = @'
{{ include (joinPath .chezmoi.sourceDir ".chezmoitemplates/agents/codex.config.overlay.toml") }}
'@
$liveText = [Console]::In.ReadToEnd()

# Empty input is a fresh install and the overlay itself is already valid TOML.
if ([string]::IsNullOrWhiteSpace($liveText)) {
    Write-StdoutBytes $utf8.GetBytes($overlayText)
    return
}

$tmpDir = [System.IO.Path]::GetTempPath()
$stamp = [System.IO.Path]::GetRandomFileName()
$overlayFile = Join-Path $tmpDir "codex-overlay-$stamp.toml"
$liveFile = Join-Path $tmpDir "codex-live-$stamp.toml"
$pyFile = Join-Path $tmpDir "codex-merge-$stamp.py"
$outFile = Join-Path $tmpDir "codex-out-$stamp.toml"

try {
    [System.IO.File]::WriteAllText($overlayFile, $overlayText, $utf8)
    [System.IO.File]::WriteAllText($liveFile, $liveText, $utf8)

    $py = $null
    if (Get-Command uv -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue) {
        $py = @('uv', 'run', '--no-project', '--quiet', '--with', 'tomlkit', '--python', '>=3.11', 'python')
    } elseif (Get-Command python -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue) {
        $py = @('python')
    } elseif (Get-Command python3 -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue) {
        $py = @('python3')
    }

    if (-not $py) {
        [Console]::Error.WriteLine('modify_config.toml: no uv/python found; preserving live config unchanged')
        Write-StdoutBytes $utf8.GetBytes($liveText)
        return
    }

    $pySource = @'
import os
import sys

import tomlkit

overlay_path = os.environ["CODEX_OVERLAY_FILE"]
live_path = os.environ["CODEX_LIVE_FILE"]
out_path = os.environ["CODEX_OUT_FILE"]

with open(overlay_path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
    overlay_text = fh.read()
with open(live_path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
    live_text = fh.read()

try:
    live = tomlkit.parse(live_text)
    overlay = tomlkit.parse(overlay_text)
except Exception as exc:
    print(f"modify_config.toml: invalid TOML; preserving live config unchanged: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)
    with open(out_path, "w", encoding="utf-8", newline="") as fh:
        fh.write(live_text)
    sys.exit(0)

if "tui" not in live or not isinstance(live["tui"], dict):
    live["tui"] = tomlkit.table()
live["tui"]["status_line"] = overlay["tui"]["status_line"]

with open(out_path, "w", encoding="utf-8", newline="") as fh:
    fh.write(tomlkit.dumps(live))
'@
    [System.IO.File]::WriteAllText($pyFile, $pySource, $utf8)

    $env:CODEX_OVERLAY_FILE = $overlayFile
    $env:CODEX_LIVE_FILE = $liveFile
    $env:CODEX_OUT_FILE = $outFile
    $exe = $py[0]
    $rest = if ($py.Count -gt 1) { @($py[1..($py.Count - 1)]) } else { @() }
    $rest += $pyFile
    & $exe @rest
    $rc = $LASTEXITCODE

    if ($rc -ne 0 -or -not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $outFile)) {
        [Console]::Error.WriteLine("modify_config.toml: merge failed (exit $rc); preserving live config unchanged")
        Write-StdoutBytes $utf8.GetBytes($liveText)
        return
    }

    Write-StdoutBytes ([System.IO.File]::ReadAllBytes($outFile))
} finally {
    foreach ($f in $overlayFile, $liveFile, $pyFile, $outFile) {
        Remove-Item -LiteralPath $f -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
    }
    foreach ($v in 'CODEX_OVERLAY_FILE', 'CODEX_LIVE_FILE', 'CODEX_OUT_FILE') {
        Remove-Item "env:$v" -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
    }
}

BeforeAll {
    $RepoRoot = Split-Path -Parent $PSScriptRoot
    $TemplatePath = Join-Path $RepoRoot 'dot_codex/modify_config.toml.ps1.tmpl'
    $RenderedPath = Join-Path $TestDrive 'modify_config.toml.ps1'
    $rendered = & chezmoi execute-template --source $RepoRoot --file $TemplatePath
    if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw 'failed to render Codex modifier' }
    [System.IO.File]::WriteAllText($RenderedPath, ($rendered -join "`n"), [System.Text.UTF8Encoding]::new($false))

    function Invoke-CodexModifier([string] $Live) {
        $stdout = $Live | & pwsh -NoProfile -NonInteractive -File $RenderedPath 2>$null
        if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw "Codex modifier failed with exit $LASTEXITCODE" }
        $stdout -join "`n"
    }
}

Describe 'Codex config overlay' {
    It 'creates the native provider-neutral status line from empty input' {
        $result = Invoke-CodexModifier ''
        $result | Should -Match '(?s)status_line\s*=.*model-with-reasoning.*fast-mode.*git-branch.*context-remaining.*task-progress.*current-dir'
        $result | Should -Not -Match 'five-hour-limit|weekly-limit'
    }

    It 'preserves providers and nested TUI keymaps while enforcing status_line' {
        $live = @'
model = "custom-model"

[model_providers.copilot]
base_url = "http://localhost:4142"

[tui]
status_line = ["current-dir"]

[tui.keymap.editor]
insert_newline = ["ctrl-j"]
'@
        $result = Invoke-CodexModifier $live
        $result | Should -Match 'model = "custom-model"'
        $result | Should -Match 'base_url = "http://localhost:4142"'
        $result | Should -Match '(?s)status_line\s*=.*model-with-reasoning.*current-dir'
        $result | Should -Match '(?s)\[tui\.keymap\.editor\].*insert_newline'
    }

    It 'fails closed by preserving malformed live TOML' {
        $live = "model = [`n"
        Invoke-CodexModifier $live | Should -Be $live
    }
}

+    function Invoke-CodexModifier {
+        param(
+            [Parameter(Mandatory)]
+            [AllowEmptyCollection()]
+            [byte[]] $LiveBytes,
+
+            [string] $ScriptPath = $RenderedPath,
+
+            [hashtable] $Environment = @{}
+        )
+
+        $startInfo = [System.Diagnostics.ProcessStartInfo]::new()
+        $startInfo.FileName = $PwshPath
+        $startInfo.UseShellExecute = $false
+        $startInfo.CreateNoWindow = $true
+        $startInfo.RedirectStandardInput = $true
+        $startInfo.RedirectStandardOutput = $true
+        $startInfo.RedirectStandardError = $true
+        $startInfo.ArgumentList.Add('-NoProfile')
+        $startInfo.ArgumentList.Add('-NonInteractive')
+        $startInfo.ArgumentList.Add('-File')
+        $startInfo.ArgumentList.Add($ScriptPath)
+        foreach ($name in $Environment.Keys) {
+            $startInfo.Environment[$name] = [string] $Environment[$name]
+        }
+
+        $process = [System.Diagnostics.Process]::new()
+        $process.StartInfo = $startInfo
+        $stdout = [System.IO.MemoryStream]::new()
+        $stderr = [System.IO.MemoryStream]::new()
+        try {
+            if (-not $process.Start()) { throw 'failed to start rendered Codex modifier' }
+            $stdoutCopy = $process.StandardOutput.BaseStream.CopyToAsync($stdout)
+            $stderrCopy = $process.StandardError.BaseStream.CopyToAsync($stderr)
+
+            if ($LiveBytes.Length -gt 0) {
+                $process.StandardInput.BaseStream.Write($LiveBytes, 0, $LiveBytes.Length)
+            }
+            $process.StandardInput.BaseStream.Close()
+
+            $process.WaitForExit()
+            $stdoutCopy.GetAwaiter().GetResult()
+            $stderrCopy.GetAwaiter().GetResult()
+
+            return [pscustomobject]@{
+                StdoutBytes = $stdout.ToArray()
+                Stderr      = $Utf8.GetString($stderr.ToArray())
+                ExitCode    = $process.ExitCode
+            }
+        } finally {
+            $stdout.Dispose()
+            $stderr.Dispose()
+            $process.Dispose()
+        }
     }
 }

1	# Copilot.psm1 — GitHub Copilot agent gateway for Claude Code and Codex, native
2	# PowerShell port of the POSIX 43_copilot_proxy.sh / 44_copilot_embed.sh.
3	#
4	# Runs the maintained copilot-api fork (npm @jeffreycao/copilot-api) from a pinned
5	# local install so a GitHub Copilot subscription can back Claude Code and Codex.
6	# The optional Bun throttle shim (copilot-throttle-shim.js) is reused verbatim from
7	# the unix side.
8	#
9	# Public commands (exported with their original hyphenated names for muscle
10	# memory — PSUseApprovedVerbs is intentionally waived):
11	#   copilot-proxy [start|stop|restart|status|doctor [--live]|logs [shim|N]|shim [on|off|status]|whoami|auth|reinstall]
12	#   copilot-run <cmd...>            run a command with the proxy env injected
13	#   claude-copilot [args...]        one-off Claude Code session on the proxy
14	#   claude-copilot-once [args...]   pinned one-shot session, auto-reverted
15	#   codex-copilot [args...]         one-off Codex session on Responses proxy
16	#   codex-copilot-once [args...]    identical zero-persistence alias
17	# (claude-copilot / -once run claude with --dangerously-skip-permissions — the
18	#  proxy flow is the trusted, hands-off path; plain `claude` is unaffected.)
19	#   copilot-here [on|off|status]    per-project pin via ./.claude/settings.local.json
20	#   copilot-model [<id>|-l|-c|--auto]  switch the pinned model
21	#   copilot-embed [--model M] [--json] [TEXT|-] | -l
22	#   semsearch index [PATH...] | semsearch <QUERY> [-k N] [--corpus PATH]
23	#
24	# Contract preserved from the unix version: token at
25	# ~/.local/share/copilot-api/github_token, ports 4141 (proxy) / 4142 (shim),
26	# state under $XDG_STATE_HOME/copilot-proxy, per-project ./.claude/settings.local.json
27	# pin, default model gpt-5.6-sol[1m], and the ANTHROPIC_* env block.
28	#
29	# The pinned package is INSTALLED ONCE into $XDG_DATA_HOME/copilot-api/pkg and the
30	# proxy runs that binary directly. It deliberately does NOT use `bunx` at launch:
31	# bunx re-resolves the package on every start, and bun stalls forever resolving
32	# through a socks proxy — which wedged `start` at "Resolving dependencies" AND kept
33	# bun's global cache lock, so every retry hung too. Force a re-install with
34	# `copilot-proxy reinstall`.
35	#
36	# Env knobs:
37	#   COPILOT_PROXY_PORT   default 4141    - port the proxy listens on
38	#   COPILOT_PROXY_START_TIMEOUT default 45 - seconds allowed for model refresh
39	#   COPILOT_SHIM_PORT    default 4142    - throttle shim port
40	#   COPILOT_API_PKG      default @jeffreycao/copilot-api@2.1.0 - spec to install
41	#                                          (changing it re-installs via the stamp)
42	#   COPILOT_CLAUDE_MODEL                 - override the pinned model
43	#   COPILOT_PROXY_QUIET  1               - add the telemetry-suppressing env keys
44	#   COPILOT_INSTALL_NOPROXY 1            - skip straight to the no-proxy install try
45	#   COPILOT_HTTP_PROXY   default auto    - Node->GitHub /models egress:
46	#                          auto   = use the Windows System Proxy (WinINET registry)
47	#                                   or HTTPS_PROXY when either is set; Node ignores
48	#                                   the system setting unless it is passed the env.
49	#                          always = same, but warn when no proxy is found
50	#                          never  = never pass --proxy-env
51	#                          http://127.0.0.1:PORT = force that URL

71	# --- pinned package install (run the binary, never `bunx` at launch) -----------
72	#
73	# Why an install prefix instead of `bunx <pkg> start`: bunx re-resolves the
74	# package on EVERY launch, and bun hangs indefinitely resolving through a socks
75	# proxy (a browser/curl through the same proxy is fine, which is what makes it so
76	# confusing). The wedged installer then keeps bun's global install-cache lock, so
77	# every retry hangs identically and stacks another zombie. Installing once and
78	# running the resulting binary removes the per-start resolve entirely — a warm
79	# start does zero network before it binds the port.
80	
81	# Package NAME without the trailing @version, keeping any @scope/ prefix.
82	# The naive "split on @" eats the whole string on a scoped spec with no version
83	# (@jeffreycao/copilot-api -> ""), so test on the scope-stripped copy.
84	function script:Get-CopilotPkgName {
85	    $spec = Get-CopilotPkg
86	    if ($spec.TrimStart('@') -match '@') { $spec -replace '@[^@]*$', '' } else { $spec }
87	}

89	function script:Get-CopilotPkgPrefix { Join-Path (Get-XdgData) 'copilot-api/pkg' }
90	# Records verified installed metadata, so bumping COPILOT_API_PKG (or the pinned
91	# default) re-installs instead of silently running an old or partial tree.
92	function script:Get-CopilotPkgStamp { Join-Path (Get-CopilotPkgPrefix) '.installed-spec' }

94	# Exact npm selectors can be verified against installed package metadata. Tags,
95	# ranges, aliases and git/file selectors are deliberately non-exact.
96	function script:Get-CopilotPkgExactVersion {
97	    $spec = Get-CopilotPkg
98	    $name = Get-CopilotPkgName
99	    if ($spec.Length -le $name.Length) { return $null }
100	    $selector = $spec.Substring($name.Length)
101	    if ($selector -match '^@v?(\d+\.\d+\.\d+(?:-[0-9A-Za-z.-]+)?(?:\+[0-9A-Za-z.-]+)?)$') {
102	        return $Matches[1]
103	    }
104	    $null
105	}

114	        [pscustomobject]@{
115	            Name    = [string]$json.name
116	            Version = [string]$json.version

158	# (plus a .bunx sidecar); the other extensions cover an npm/yarn-populated prefix.

170	# How to invoke the installed proxy: @{ Exe; Pre; Cwd }. Cwd is non-null only for

172	#

181	    if ($bin -and [System.IO.Path]::GetExtension($bin) -in '.exe', '.cmd', '.bat') {

183	    }

213	# Remove only the requested package and its dedicated launch shims. This ensures a
214	# failed ETARGET/install cannot pass its postcondition by inheriting an old tree.
215	function script:Clear-CopilotPkgInstallTarget {
216	    $packageDir = Join-Path (Get-CopilotPkgPrefix) "node_modules/$(Get-CopilotPkgName)"
217	    Remove-Item -LiteralPath $packageDir -Recurse -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
218	    $binDir = Join-Path (Get-CopilotPkgPrefix) 'node_modules/.bin'

225	# One package-install attempt in -Dir, bounded by -BudgetSeconds. npm is preferred
226	# because it supports Azure Artifacts' credential-provider token in ~/.npmrc;
227	# Bun does not. -NoProxy strips the proxy env for the child. Returns $true only
228	# when matching metadata and a runnable launch path exist afterwards.
229	#
230	# Success is judged from the FILESYSTEM, not $p.ExitCode: a Start-Process -PassThru
231	# object reports ExitCode 0 even for a child that exited non-zero (verified — the
232	# .Handle-caching workaround does not help either), so trusting it would let a
233	# failed install write the .installed-spec stamp and silently pin a broken prefix.
234	#
235	# The kill on expiry is the load-bearing part: a stalled `bun add` left running
236	# keeps bun's global install-cache lock, and THAT is what made every subsequent
237	# start hang too. Never let one escape.
238	function script:Invoke-CopilotPkgInstallTry {
239	    param([string] $Dir, [switch] $NoProxy, [int] $BudgetSeconds)
240	
241	    Clear-CopilotPkgInstallTarget
242	    $proxyVars = 'ALL_PROXY', 'all_proxy', 'HTTP_PROXY', 'http_proxy', 'HTTPS_PROXY', 'https_proxy'
243	    $npm = Get-Command npm.cmd -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
244	    $installer = if ($npm) {
245	        @{ File = $npm.Source; Args = @('install', '--no-save', '--no-audit', '--no-fund', (Get-CopilotPkg)) }
246	    } else {
247	        Write-Warning 'copilot-proxy: npm.cmd not found; falling back to Bun (authenticated Azure Artifacts feeds require npm).'
248	        @{ File = 'bun'; Args = @('add', (Get-CopilotPkg), '--no-summary') }
249	    }
250	    $saved = @{}
251	    if ($NoProxy) {
252	        foreach ($v in $proxyVars) { $saved[$v] = [Environment]::GetEnvironmentVariable($v); Remove-Item "env:$v" -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue }
253	    }
254	    try {
255	        $p = Start-Process -FilePath $installer.File -ArgumentList $installer.Args `
256	            -WorkingDirectory $Dir -PassThru -NoNewWindow -ErrorAction Stop
257	        if ($p.WaitForExit($BudgetSeconds * 1000)) { return (Test-CopilotPkgInstalled) }
258	        Stop-Process -Id $p.Id -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
259	        # The subshell's child is the one actually holding the install lock.
260	        $name = [regex]::Escape((Get-CopilotPkgName))
261	        Get-CimInstance Win32_Process -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue |
262	            Where-Object { $_.Name -in 'bun.exe', 'node.exe' -and $_.CommandLine -match '\b(add|install)\b' -and $_.CommandLine -match $name } |
263	            ForEach-Object { Stop-Process -Id $_.ProcessId -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue }
264	        return $false
265	    } catch {
266	        Write-Error "copilot-proxy: could not launch package installer ($_)"; return $false
267	    } finally {
268	        if ($NoProxy) {
269	            foreach ($v in $proxyVars) {
270	                if ($null -eq $saved[$v]) { Remove-Item "env:$v" -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue }
271	                else { Set-Item "env:$v" $saved[$v] }
272	            }
273	        }
274	    }
275	}

277	# Ensure the pinned spec is installed. No-op (and no network) once it is.
278	function script:Install-CopilotPkg {
279	    if (Test-CopilotPkgReady) { return $true }
280	
281	    # Migrate the old one-line stamp without a network call only when an exact
282	    # selector, the legacy stamp, live package metadata and launch path all agree.
283	    $metadata = Get-CopilotPkgMetadata
284	    if ((Get-CopilotPkgExactVersion) -and
285	        (Get-CopilotPkgLegacyStamp) -ceq (Get-CopilotPkg) -and
286	        (Test-CopilotPkgInstalled -Metadata $metadata)) {
287	        Write-CopilotPkgStamp -Metadata $metadata

289	    }
290	
291	    if (-not (Get-Command bun -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue)) {
292	        Write-Error "copilot-proxy: bun not found (scoop install bun)"; return $false
293	    }
294	    $spec = Get-CopilotPkg; $prefix = Get-CopilotPkgPrefix
295	    New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path $prefix | Out-Null
296	    # A private package.json keeps `bun add` from walking up and polluting $HOME.
297	    $pkgJson = Join-Path $prefix 'package.json'
298	    if (-not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $pkgJson)) {
299	        '{"name":"copilot-api-runner","private":true,"version":"0.0.0"}' | Set-Content -Path $pkgJson -Encoding utf8
300	    }

302	    Write-Host "copilot-proxy: installing $spec (one-time — later starts skip this) ..."
303	    # Attempt 1 honours the ambient env: on a host where the npm registry is only
304	    # reachable THROUGH the proxy, stripping it would break the install. Attempt 2
305	    # strips it, which is what rescues the socks stall. COPILOT_INSTALL_NOPROXY=1
306	    # skips straight to attempt 2 (saves the 45s stall on a known-bad host).
307	    $skipFirst = ($env:COPILOT_INSTALL_NOPROXY -eq '1')
308	    if ($skipFirst -or -not (Invoke-CopilotPkgInstallTry -Dir $prefix -BudgetSeconds 45)) {
309	        if (-not $skipFirst) {
310	            Write-Warning "copilot-proxy: install failed or stalled with the proxy env — retrying without it ..."
311	            # Drop bun's cache lock dir before retrying; the killed attempt may have
312	            # left it behind, and a stale lock hangs the retry for the same reason.
313	            $bunHome = if ($env:BUN_INSTALL) { $env:BUN_INSTALL } else { Join-Path $HOME '.bun' }
314	            Remove-Item -Recurse -Force (Join-Path $bunHome 'install/cache/.tmp') -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
315	        }
316	        if (-not (Invoke-CopilotPkgInstallTry -Dir $prefix -NoProxy -BudgetSeconds 90)) {
317	            Write-Error "copilot-proxy: could not install $spec — run 'copilot-proxy doctor'."; return $false
318	        }
319	    }
320	
321	    $metadata = Get-CopilotPkgMetadata
322	    if (-not (Test-CopilotPkgInstalled -Metadata $metadata)) {
323	        $actual = if ($metadata) { "$($metadata.Name)@$($metadata.Version)" } else { 'no readable package metadata' }
324	        Write-Error "copilot-proxy: install finished but $actual does not satisfy $spec with a runnable launch path under $prefix."
325	        return $false
326	    }
327	    Write-CopilotPkgStamp -Metadata $metadata
328	    $true
329	}

331	# Run a copilot-api subcommand (auth / check-usage / debug) in the foreground.
332	# Honours $launch.Cwd so the `bun run` fallback resolves node_modules/.bin.
333	function script:Invoke-CopilotPkgCommand {
334	    param([Parameter(ValueFromRemainingArguments)] [string[]] $Argument)
335	    if (-not (Install-CopilotPkg)) { return }
336	    $launch = Get-CopilotPkgLaunch
337	    if (-not $launch) { Write-Error "copilot-proxy: no runnable copilot-api — try 'copilot-proxy reinstall'"; return }
338	    if ($launch.Cwd) { Push-Location $launch.Cwd }
339	    try {
340	        & $launch.Exe @($launch.Pre + $Argument)
341	        $commandExitCode = $LASTEXITCODE
342	        $global:LASTEXITCODE = $commandExitCode
343	        if ($commandExitCode -ne 0) {
344	            Write-Error "copilot-proxy: copilot-api $($Argument -join ' ') failed with exit code $commandExitCode"
345	        }
346	    } finally { if ($launch.Cwd) { Pop-Location } }
347	}

349	# Live `bun add … copilot-api` processes. Install is a one-shot, so a match at
350	# rest is a clean stale-installer signal: a stalled one keeps bun's global
351	# install-cache lock, which wedges every later install too. Invoke-CopilotPkgInstallTry
352	# bounds and kills its own attempts, so this should stay empty — it remains as a
353	# safety net for a stall we didn't spawn (e.g. a hand-run `bunx @jeffreycao/copilot-api`).
354	function script:Get-CopilotStaleInstaller {
355	    Get-CimInstance Win32_Process -Filter "Name = 'bun.exe'" -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue |
356	        Where-Object { $_.CommandLine -match '\badd\b' -and $_.CommandLine -match 'copilot-api' }
357	}

369	# --- egress: which proxy should Node use for the GitHub /models fetch? --------
370	#
371	# copilot-api fetches /models at startup and refreshes its cache periodically;
372	# restart forces an immediate refresh. GitHub geo-filters the Claude catalog on
373	# some egress paths. Node does NOT honour the Windows System Proxy on its own — it
374	# only sees HTTP(S)_PROXY — so a host whose browser reaches the unfiltered catalog
375	# could still have the proxy cache a Claude-less list, which then looks exactly
376	# like an entitlement problem. Resolve the URL here and hand it to the child.
377	#
378	# COPILOT_HTTP_PROXY: auto|always|never|<url>. Returns a URL or $null.
379	function script:Resolve-CopilotHttpProxy {
380	    $mode = if ($env:COPILOT_HTTP_PROXY) { $env:COPILOT_HTTP_PROXY } else { 'auto' }
381	    switch -Regex ($mode) {
382	        '^(never|off|0|false|no)$' { return $null }
383	        '^(http|https|socks5h?)://' { return $mode }
384	        '^(always|auto|on|1|true|yes)$' { break }
385	        default {
386	            Write-Warning "copilot-proxy: unknown COPILOT_HTTP_PROXY='$mode' (use auto|always|never|http://...)"
387	            return $null
388	        }
389	    }
390	
391	    # The Windows System Proxy (WinINET). This is what Clash Verge / mihomo /
392	    # v2rayN write when their "System Proxy" toggle is on, so reading it covers
393	    # the same ground the unix side gets from its Clash detector.
394	    try {
395	        $key = Get-ItemProperty -Path 'HKCU:\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Internet Settings' -ErrorAction Stop
396	        if ($key.ProxyEnable -eq 1 -and $key.ProxyServer) {
397	            # ProxyServer is either "host:port" or "http=host:port;https=host:port".
398	            $server = $key.ProxyServer
399	            if ($server -match '(?:^|;)\s*https?=([^;]+)') { $server = $Matches[1] }
400	            elseif ($server -match ';') { $server = ($server -split ';')[0] }
401	            if ($server) { return "http://$($server -replace '^https?://', '')" }
402	        }
403	    } catch { $null = $_ }
404	
405	    # Fallback: an explicit env proxy in this shell.
406	    foreach ($v in $env:HTTPS_PROXY, $env:https_proxy, $env:HTTP_PROXY, $env:http_proxy) {
407	        if ($v) { return $v }
408	    }
409	    $null
410	}

412	# Model ids GitHub serves for this account RIGHT NOW, for the direct-vs-proxied
413	# A/B in doctor. -Via: 'direct' forces no proxy, a URL forces that proxy, absent
414	# uses .NET defaults. Returns sorted-unique ids, or $null on any failure.
415	#
416	# Secrets: the ghu_/bearer tokens only ever travel in request headers — never in
417	# a command line, never echoed.
418	function script:Get-CopilotUpstreamModel {
419	    param([string] $Via)
420	
421	    $tokFile = Get-CopilotToken
422	    if (-not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $tokFile)) { return $null }
423	    $ghu = Get-Content -First 1 $tokFile -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
424	    if (-not $ghu) { return $null }
425	
426	    $transport = @{}
427	    if ($Via -eq 'direct') { $transport['NoProxy'] = $true }
428	    elseif ($Via) { $transport['Proxy'] = $Via }
429	
430	    try {
431	        $ex = Invoke-RestMethod -Uri 'https://api.github.com/copilot_internal/v2/token' -TimeoutSec 10 `
432	            -Headers @{ 'Authorization' = "token $ghu"; 'user-agent' = 'GitHubCopilotChat/0.26.7' } `
433	            @transport -ErrorAction Stop
434	    } catch { return $null }
435	
436	    $api = if ($ex.endpoints.api) { $ex.endpoints.api } else { 'https://api.githubcopilot.com' }
437	    if (-not $ex.token) { return $null }
438	
439	    try {
440	        $up = Invoke-RestMethod -Uri "$api/models" -TimeoutSec 12 `
441	            -Headers @{
442	                'Authorization'            = "Bearer $($ex.token)"
443	                'user-agent'               = 'GitHubCopilotChat/0.26.7'
444	                'copilot-integration-id'   = 'vscode-chat'
445	            } @transport -ErrorAction Stop
446	    } catch { return $null }
447	
448	    @($up.data.id | Where-Object { $_ } | Sort-Object -Unique)
449	}

451	# Optional ChatGPT Apps reachability. This is deliberately separate from the
452	# Copilot inference probes: codex_apps is a remote MCP served by chatgpt.com,
453	# not a localhost bridge to Codex.app and not part of GitHub Copilot.
454	function script:Get-CopilotProbeFailureKind {
455	    param($ErrorRecord)
456	
457	    $message = if ($ErrorRecord -is [System.Management.Automation.ErrorRecord]) {
458	        $ErrorRecord.Exception.ToString()
459	    } else { [string]$ErrorRecord }
460	
461	    if ($message -match '(?i)timed?\s*out|timeout|operation.*canceled|deadline') { return 'timeout' }
462	    if ($message -match '(?i)certificate|authenticationexception|ssl|tls|secure channel') { return 'tls' }
463	    'network'
464	}

466	function script:Invoke-CopilotOptionalHttpProbe {
467	    param(
468	        [Parameter(Mandatory)] [string] $Uri,
469	        [string] $Via = 'direct'
470	    )
471	
472	    $transport = @{}
473	    if ($Via -eq 'direct') { $transport['NoProxy'] = $true }
474	    elseif ($Via) { $transport['Proxy'] = $Via }
475	
476	    $sw = [System.Diagnostics.Stopwatch]::StartNew()
477	    try {
478	        $response = Invoke-WebRequest -Uri $Uri -Method Get -TimeoutSec 12 `
479	            -SkipHttpErrorCheck -Headers @{ 'user-agent' = 'codex-copilot-doctor/1.0' } `
480	            @transport -ErrorAction Stop
481	        $sw.Stop()
482	        [pscustomobject]@{
483	            Reached = $true
484	            Code    = [int]$response.StatusCode
485	            Seconds = [math]::Round($sw.Elapsed.TotalSeconds, 2)
486	            Kind    = $null
487	            Error   = $null
488	        }
489	    } catch {
490	        $sw.Stop()
491	        [pscustomobject]@{
492	            Reached = $false
493	            Code    = 0
494	            Seconds = [math]::Round($sw.Elapsed.TotalSeconds, 2)
495	            Kind    = Get-CopilotProbeFailureKind $_
496	            Error   = ($_.Exception.Message -replace '\s+', ' ').Trim()
497	        }
498	    }
499	}

525	# Resolve the model: $COPILOT_CLAUDE_MODEL > state file > default.
526	#
527	#   - HYPHENATED ids (claude-opus-4-8), not dotted (claude-opus-4.8): Claude Code
528	#     only recognizes hyphenated family names — dotted ids fall back to a legacy
529	#     "[Opus 4] retired" label AND a 200k context assumption.
530	#   - "[1m]" suffix: Claude Code uses it to size HUD/compaction for a 1M context
531	#     window. ConvertTo-CopilotClaudeModel derives it from live /v1/models metadata
532	#     for every provider. Claude Code-only: raw API clients use the plain id.
533	function script:Get-CopilotDefaultModel {
534	    if ($env:COPILOT_CLAUDE_MODEL) { return $env:COPILOT_CLAUDE_MODEL }
535	    $sf = Get-CopilotModelState
536	    if (Test-Path $sf) { return (Get-Content -First 1 $sf) }
537	    'gpt-5.6-sol[1m]'
538	}

540	# Every model id the proxy accepts: .id plus the .claude_model_id alias. Callers
541	# with several catalog views pass one snapshot so all decisions share one response.
542	function script:Get-CopilotServedModels {
543	    param($Catalog)
544	    if (-not $PSBoundParameters.ContainsKey('Catalog')) { $Catalog = Get-CopilotModelCatalog }
545	    if (-not $Catalog) { return @() }
546	    $ids = [System.Collections.Generic.List[string]]::new()
547	    foreach ($m in $Catalog.data) {
548	        if ($m.id) { $ids.Add([string]$m.id) }
549	        if ($m.claude_model_id) { $ids.Add([string]$m.claude_model_id) }
550	    }
551	    $ids | Sort-Object -Unique
552	}

572	# Pick exactly one live inference target. The configured main wins only when its
573	# raw id is advertised; otherwise the catalog-ranked fallback is explicit.
574	function script:Resolve-CopilotDoctorTarget {
575	    param([string] $ConfiguredMain, [string[]] $RawModel)
576	    $RawModel = @($RawModel | Where-Object { $_ -and $_ -notmatch 'embedding' } | Sort-Object -Unique)
577	    $rawConfigured = Remove-CopilotContextHint $ConfiguredMain
578	    if ($rawConfigured -and $RawModel -contains $rawConfigured) {
579	        return [pscustomobject]@{
580	            Model  = $rawConfigured
581	            Label  = 'ConfiguredMain'
582	            Reason = 'configured main is advertised by the live catalog'
583	        }
584	    }
585	
586	    $fallback = Select-CopilotBestModel -Model $RawModel
587	    $reason = if ($rawConfigured) {
588	        "configured main '$rawConfigured' is not advertised by the live catalog"
589	    } else {
590	        'no configured main model was found'
591	    }
592	    [pscustomobject]@{
593	        Model  = $fallback
594	        Label  = 'CatalogFallback'
595	        Reason = $reason
596	    }
597	}

599	function script:ConvertTo-CopilotCompactText {
600	    param($Value, [int] $MaxLength = 320)
601	    $text = if ($Value -is [string]) { $Value } else {
602	        try { $Value | ConvertTo-Json -Depth 12 -Compress -ErrorAction Stop } catch { [string]$Value }
603	    }
604	    $text = ($text -replace '\s+', ' ').Trim()
605	    if ($text.Length -gt $MaxLength) { return $text.Substring(0, $MaxLength - 3) + '...' }
606	    $text
607	}

609	# Error bodies appear as direct code/message pairs, error.code/error.message, or
610	# another JSON error encoded inside error.message. Normalize all three shapes.
611	function script:Get-CopilotApiError {
612	    param($Body, [int] $Depth = 0)
613	    $raw = ConvertTo-CopilotCompactText $Body
614	    if ($Depth -gt 4) {
615	        return [pscustomobject]@{ Code = $null; Message = $null; Raw = $raw }
616	    }
617	
618	    $object = $Body
619	    if ($Body -is [string]) {
620	        try { $object = $Body | ConvertFrom-Json -ErrorAction Stop }
621	        catch { return [pscustomobject]@{ Code = $null; Message = $null; Raw = $raw } }
622	    }
623	    if (-not $object) { return [pscustomobject]@{ Code = $null; Message = $null; Raw = $raw } }
624	
625	    $container = $object
626	    if ($object.PSObject.Properties['error']) {
627	        $container = $object.error
628	        if ($container -is [string]) {
629	            $nestedError = Get-CopilotApiError -Body $container -Depth ($Depth + 1)
630	            if ($nestedError.Code -or $nestedError.Message) { return $nestedError }
631	        }
632	    }
633	
634	    $code = if ($container.PSObject.Properties['code']) { [string]$container.code } else { $null }
635	    $message = if ($container.PSObject.Properties['message']) { [string]$container.message } else { $null }
636	    if ($message -and $message.TrimStart().StartsWith('{')) {
637	        $nestedMessage = Get-CopilotApiError -Body $message -Depth ($Depth + 1)
638	        if ($nestedMessage.Code -or $nestedMessage.Message) { return $nestedMessage }
639	    }
640	    [pscustomobject]@{ Code = $code; Message = $message; Raw = $raw }
641	}
642	
643	function script:Classify-CopilotInferenceError {
644	    param([int] $StatusCode, $Body)
645	    $errorInfo = Get-CopilotApiError -Body $Body
646	    $code = ([string]$errorInfo.Code).ToLowerInvariant()
647	    $detailParts = @($errorInfo.Code, $errorInfo.Message) | Where-Object { $_ }
648	    $detail = $detailParts -join ': '
649	    if (-not $detail) { $detail = $errorInfo.Raw }
650	
651	    if ($StatusCode -eq 402 -and $code -eq 'billing_not_configured') {
652	        return [pscustomobject]@{
653	            Kind        = 'BillingNotConfigured'
654	            Code        = $errorInfo.Code
655	            Message     = $errorInfo.Message
656	            Summary     = "account-wide GitHub Copilot billing is not configured: $detail"
657	            Retryable   = $false
658	            AccountWide = $true
659	            Action      = 'https://github.com/settings/copilot/features'
660	            Guidance    = 'Select an organization or enterprise in GitHub''s "Usage billed to" setting. Changing the model, using --auto, or enabling the shim cannot fix this account-wide failure.'
661	        }
662	    }
663	
664	    if ($code -match '^(model_not_supported|model_unsupported|unsupported_model)$') {
665	        return [pscustomobject]@{
666	            Kind        = 'ModelUnsupported'
667	            Code        = $errorInfo.Code
668	            Message     = $errorInfo.Message
669	            Summary     = $detail
670	            Retryable   = $false
671	            AccountWide = $false
672	            Action      = 'Run copilot-model --auto, or copilot-model -l and select a model advertised by the live catalog.'
673	            Guidance    = $null
674	        }
675	    }
676	
677	    [pscustomobject]@{
678	        Kind        = 'HttpError'
679	        Code        = $errorInfo.Code
680	        Message     = $errorInfo.Message
681	        Summary     = $detail
682	        Retryable   = ($StatusCode -eq 429 -or $StatusCode -ge 500)
683	        AccountWide = $false
684	        Action      = $null
685	        Guidance    = $null
686	    }
687	}
